About the Role

We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineer focused on AI architecture research to help design, prototype, and validate next-generation model architectures. You’ll work at the intersection of research and production — turning new ideas into scalable, real-world systems.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys questioning architectural assumptions, experimenting with novel model designs, and pushing beyond standard Transformer-style approaches.

What You’ll Work On

  • Prototype models end-to-end — from research code to training-ready implementations

  • Collaborate with inference and systems engineers to ensure architectures are deployable and efficient

  • Analyze model behavior, failure modes, and inductive biases

  • Read, reproduce, and extend cutting-edge research papers

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong background in machine learning fundamentals and deep learning

  • Hands-on experience implementing model architectures from scratch

  • Solid understanding of:

    • Attention mechanisms, RNNs, state-space models, or hybrid architectures

    • Training dynamics, scaling behavior, and optimization

    • Memory, latency, and compute constraints at the model level

  • Comfortable working in PyTorch or JAX

  • Ability to move fluidly between theory, experimentation, and engineering

  • Clear communicator who can explain architectural trade-offs

Nice to Have

  • Experience with non-Transformer architectures (RNN variants, SSMs, long-context models)

  • Background in research-driven startups or open-source ML projects

  • Experience with large-scale training or custom training loops

  • Publications, preprints, or notable research contributions

  • Familiarity with inference optimization and deployment constraints

Why Join

  • Work on core model architecture, not just fine-tuning

  • Direct influence on the technical direction of a Series-A company

  • Small, high-caliber team with fast feedback loops

  • Opportunity to ship research into production

  • Competitive compensation + meaningful equity

jobs.title: Hands-on Engineering Manager (C#/Vue)
jobs.description:
Location: 100% remote (EMEA + South America)

Classification: Full-time

Pay Range: €82,000–140,000; determined by several factors, including location

Miaplaza is looking for two Engineering Managers to lead two of our software development teams. We’re hiring for one existing team of 7 engineers and one new team that we will hire developers into.

This is a management role for someone who wants to grow as a manager while still remaining hands-on with code. You'll split your time roughly 50/50 between leading your team and doing hands-on work alongside them.

About Miaplaza

Miaplaza is dedicated to making education engaging and accessible through innovative online learning platforms. We develop personalized learning experiences for students, helping them grow in a supportive and interactive environment. Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive education curriculum platform where all students can be successful!

As an engineering manager at Miaplaza, your team will build technology with a direct impact on the lives of hundreds of thousands of students. Every step of the way, you will have the opportunity to influence our direction. Through our platforms, we create engaging, safe, and thoughtfully designed learning experiences that help children grow academically, creatively, and personally. Every feature we ship, every system we scale, and every improvement we make contributes to shaping how the next generation learns and discovers their potential. If our platform is down, a child might not go to school that day. We’re looking for leaders who want their work to matter in classrooms and homes, who care about access to quality education, and who are excited to craft technology that makes a difference in young people’s lives. Here, your impact doesn’t just power a product; it shapes future generations!

What you’ll work on

We’re a C# and platform growing towards a scale that no longer matches our legacy architecture. You’ll need to work with your team balancing both product and engineering initiatives. You’ll report to our head of engineering and be expected to split your time roughly 50/50 between people management and hands-on development. Prioritization always goes to leading and supporting your engineers.

How management works at Miaplaza

We're a US-based company, so this may differ from what you've done before:

  1. You start as an engineer. You’ll onboard as a senior engineer on your own team for two months, begin manager onboarding in month two, and take over the team at around week 10. Both phases matter equally, and this isn’t negotiable.

  2. You stay hands-on. Around 50% of your time stays hands-on after onboarding, but leading and supporting your engineers always comes first.

  3. You teach. Growing your engineers and those around you is a core responsibility. You'll have full oversight of your direct reports' work, because you can't teach well without seeing the process behind the output.

  4. Feedback is the norm. You'll give specific reinforcement and constructive feedback whenever you notice something, and you'll receive it too.

Requirements

What you must bring

We can only move forward with candidates who meet these requirements:

  • 7+ years of experience in software development in one or more object-oriented programming languages

  • 3+ years of experience with front-end software development in a reactive front-end framework

  • 3+ years of experience with software architecture

  • 3+ years of experience operating at a Senior, Staff, or Principal Engineer level

  • 2+ years of experience being a mentor/leader

  • 1+ years leading a team, formally or as a tech lead

  • Experience working directly with product and design on scoping and prioritization

  • Experience being on-call and resolving production incidents

  • A bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

What makes you stand out

  • Experience leading a team through a significant architectural migration

  • Experience with consumer platforms at scale

  • Experience building in regulated environments

  • Experience with DevOps technologies (eg K8s, IaC, sysadmin, build pipelines, etc.)

  • Extensive senior front-end development experience

Responsibilities

  • Work with your teams to design, develop, and maintain scalable and reliable web applications using primarily C# and Vue.js

  • Collaborate with your product trio (PM, UX, EM), product leadership team, and other EMs to scope, prioritize, and deliver features that matter to students and families

  • Set the quality bar for your team. You'll have dedicated capacity for reliability and architecture work rather than fitting it around feature delivery, and a strong say in where that capacity goes.

  • Manage, lead, and mentor your team while working side by side with them in code quality, clean architecture, soft skills, best practices, etc

  • Lead team trainings, set SMART goals, hold performance reviews, and provide individual feedback recurrently to each of your devs

Our hiring process

As a remote company, we receive a large number of applicants, so our process is longer than usual. At every stage we try to respect your time.

  1. Application and CV review. We review your application answers and CV, then follow up with an update.

  2. Initial technical screen (20 min). A few administrative questions and short technical questions related to the role.

  3. Behavioral interview (1 hour). With a member of our HR team, about your experience and approach so far.

  4. 1st technical interview (1 hour). With a member of the engineering team to answer technical questions tailored to our work.

  5. 2nd technical interview (1 hour). With a member of the engineering team to dive into a hypothetical scenario and how you’d tackle it.

  6. Leadership interview (1 hour). With our Head of Engineering or executive leadership.

  7. Reference check. We contact the 3 references you provide, including at least one former or current manager, a colleague, and a former or current direct report.

  8. Offer and background check. Once you sign your offer, we run a background check in accordance with applicable law.

We give honest, timely feedback at every step. Job searches are hard; we don't want to make yours harder.

Compensation

The pay range for this role is €82,000 - 140,000. Our compensation philosophy aims for equity and competitiveness while considering regional differences in labor costs. Placement in the range depends on demonstrated skills, internal equity and local labor market rates for your area.

Miaplaza is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds. If you need accommodations at any point in the process, just let us know.

jobs.title: Full-Charge Bookkeeper — QuickBooks Expert
jobs.description:
About ERPS Group

ERPS Group is a fast-growing accounting, tax, and business advisory firm dedicated to helping business owners build stronger, more profitable companies. We provide accounting, tax planning, bookkeeping, payroll, CFO advisory, and business consulting services to clients across multiple industries.
Our mission is to deliver exceptional client service while helping entrepreneurs make informed financial decisions and achieve long-term success. We believe in professionalism, accountability, continuous improvement, and teamwork. Every member of our team plays an important role in creating an outstanding client experience.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Full-Charge Bookkeeper who can independently manage the day-to-day bookkeeping operations of a U.S.-based company.
The ideal candidate is highly experienced with QuickBooks Online/Desktop (QBO, QBD) and understands bookkeeping from end to end — including Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, invoicing, reconciliations, financial reporting, and month-end closing.
This is not a data-entry position. We need someone who understands why transactions are recorded a certain way, can identify discrepancies, and can maintain accurate and organized financial records with minimal supervision.

Key Responsibilities

QuickBooks & Bookkeeping
- Manage the company’s bookkeeping activities in QuickBooks.
- Record and categorize daily financial transactions accurately.
- Maintain the chart of accounts and ensure transactions are properly classified.
- Perform bank and credit card reconciliations.
- Review accounts for discrepancies, duplicates, missing transactions, and unusual activity.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial records.

Accounts Payable
- Manage vendor bills and accounts payable.
- Enter, categorize, and track bills in QuickBooks.
- Monitor outstanding payables and payment due dates.
- Verify invoices and supporting documentation.
- Maintain accurate vendor records.
- Assist with payment processing and AP reporting.

Accounts Receivable & Invoicing
- Create and send customer invoices.
- Track outstanding invoices and accounts receivable.
- Apply customer payments accurately.
- Follow up on overdue invoices when required.
- Reconcile customer accounts and resolve discrepancies.
- Maintain accurate customer records.

Month-End & Financial Reporting
- Complete monthly bank, credit card, AP, and AR reconciliations.
- Assist with month-end closing procedures.
- Prepare and maintain monthly financial statements, including:
- Profit & Loss
- Balance Sheet
- Accounts Receivable Aging
- Accounts Payable Aging
- Cash flow reports
- Identify unusual fluctuations and communicate potential issues to management.
- Provide clean and accurate financial information for management and tax/accounting purposes.

Requirements

3+ years of hands-on bookkeeping experience, preferably supporting U.S.-based businesses.
Advanced knowledge of QuickBooks Online/Desktop.
Strong understanding of double-entry bookkeeping and accounting principles.
Strong experience with Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable.
Proven experience with invoicing and payment tracking.
Strong bank and credit card reconciliation experience.
Experience with month-end closing and financial reporting.
Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to identify errors and discrepancies rather than simply entering data.
Excellent English written communication skills.
Ability to work independently and meet deadlines.
Reliable internet connection and a professional home-office setup.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with U.S. companies and U.S. accounting practices.
Experience with service-based businesses.
Experience working with multiple entities or businesses.
Familiarity with payroll transactions and payroll reconciliations.
Familiarity with sales tax accounting.
Experience working alongside CPAs, tax preparers, or CFOs.
QuickBooks Online certification is a plus.

What We Are Looking For

We are looking for someone who is:
Detail-oriented — small discrepancies do not get overlooked.
Proactive — you identify problems before they become bigger problems.
Accountable — you take ownership of your work and deadlines.
Organized — financial records are clean, structured, and easy to understand.
Analytical — you understand the numbers rather than simply entering transactions.
Independent — you can manage your responsibilities without constant supervision.
Confidential and trustworthy — you will be working with sensitive financial information.

Performance Expectations

Success in this role means:
Books are accurate and up to date.
Bank and credit card accounts are reconciled consistently.
AP and AR are properly maintained.
Invoices are issued accurately and on time.
Outstanding receivables are actively monitored.
Month-end closing is completed on schedule.
Financial reports are accurate and reliable.
Errors and discrepancies are identified and resolved promptly.
Management can rely on the bookkeeping records to make business decisions.

How to Apply

Please submit your resume and a 1-min video explaining why you’re the perfect fit for this role. We're looking for a driven leader ready to help us 10X our impact while creating transformational results for our clients and team.

IMPORTANT: Please do not apply if you only have basic QuickBooks or data-entry experience. We are specifically looking for a strong, hands-on full-charge bookkeeper who can own the bookkeeping function.

jobs.title: Cloud Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
About the Role

As a Cloud Platform Engineer at Supabase, you’ll join Cloud Engineering, part of Engineering Operations, and shape the foundations that let engineering teams build, ship, and operate infrastructure safely and independently across AWS and GCP.

This is a role spanning cloud governance, platform engineering, and hands-on operations. You’ll work across AWS and GCP account structure, identity and access management, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), reusable platform primitives, security boundaries, and self-service workflows for engineers.

You’ll be joining at a point where many of these foundations are being actively defined or reworked. We’re looking for someone who can take ambiguous, messy, business-critical infrastructure problems and turn them into pragmatic systems, tools, standards, and written guidance that scale with the company and empower teams to go faster.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

  • Designing and implementing cloud governance across AWS and GCP, including identity, account organization, access controls, and guardrails.

  • Building reusable infrastructure and building blocks using Infrastructure as Code (IaC), enabling teams to provision and manage infrastructure safely and consistently.

  • Creating self-service capabilities that reduce organizational friction and let engineers move more quickly within sensible boundaries.

  • Owning resource governance and visibility: management tagging, a trustworthy inventory of what exists and who owns it, and consistent cross-account billing data.

  • Developing reusable security primitives, including secrets storage, KMS, certificate management, token vending, direct service-to-service authentication, mTLS, and related platform services.

  • Owning cloud-level network and operational primitives: IP address management, DNS, and health signals such as service-limit and quota alerting.

  • Combining software engineering with hands-on operations and total ownership: building, deploying, monitoring, troubleshooting, and improving what you own.

  • Establishing and sharing cloud engineering best practices through documentation, internal tooling, examples, and enablement.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have 5+ years of experience in cloud governance, platform engineering, and/or operations, have operated production systems at scale, and carried on-call for them.

  • Have previously undertaken a significant migration, e.g. rearchitected an AWS account topology, introduced IaC for existing infrastructure, centralized identity/SSO, or brought a second cloud under governance.

  • Enjoy building internal platform and self-service experiences for other engineers.

  • Are genuinely deep in at least one—ideally two—of the three strength areas below (and tell us which is your center of gravity):

    • Tooling & ecosystem: You’re intimately familiar with the breadth of AWS services in general, and IAM/SSO in particular. You know their Well-Architected Framework, and when to reach outside. You have working knowledge of GCP. You use IaC routinely and have run it in production, whichever tool. You’ve probably collaborated with auditors on meeting compliance requirements.

    • Software engineering: You write real production code (Go, Rust, or a comparable systems language), and can build reliable, maintainable services. You thrive across all stages of the SDLC, set technical direction, know how to de-risk projects, and produce written artifacts such as RFCs.

    • Operations: You’ve run production infrastructure yourself: carried the pager, written the alerts and runbooks, used SLOs or similar to decide what to fix first, and made shared systems less risky over time. You like owning systems, simplifying complex infrastructure problems, and turning best practices into reusable building blocks.

  • Are comfortable treating infrastructure as software and have relevant experience with IaC and automation.

  • Communicate clearly, work with a wide range of stakeholders, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

  • Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and iterating toward better systems over time.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

If you're seeking end-to-end ownership of your work, you've come to the right place!

Your Team and Role

Working on the Security Functional Team, you'll play a pivotal role in ensuring our security capabilities keep pace with our rapid product development, including our expanding AI offerings like Duck.ai and agentic browsing, directly protecting our users across all our products. You'll also maintain incident detection and response capabilities for the company, and work on related projects. Recent projects include:

  • Browser and sync security audits

  • SERP security mitigations

  • Agentic browser hardening

As a Senior Web Security Engineer, Browser Platform, you'll harden our agentic browsing and DuckAI experiences against emerging threats (like prompt injection), conduct browser and sync security audits (special pages, DuckAI integrations, password manager, etc.), execute on SERP security mitigations (XSS prevention, tooling development to help engineers write safer code), build and maintain harnesses that get security fixes out automatically, manage application security scanning infrastructure setup, deliver on internal red-team operations (simulated attack scenarios), support security triage, and more!

jobs.description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week

Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.

Check out this Loom video for more details:

We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.

This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.

What this role actually is

You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:

• Whether the response makes sense

  • Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
  • Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
  • Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.

What you'll be doing

  • Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
  • Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
  • Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
  • Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
  • Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
  • Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code

What we mean by "taste"

We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

  • Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
  • Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
  • Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
  • Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.

Who you are

  • Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
  • Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
  • Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
  • Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
  • Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
  • Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
  • Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
  • High bar for what good engineering looks like

Nice to have

  • Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
  • Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards

Engagement details

  • Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location

• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible

  • Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
  • Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
  • Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

jobs.title: QA Automation Engineer, Mobile Games - Freelance
jobs.description:
Empire: Four Kingdoms launched in January 2013 and is the world’s all-time highest-grossing app produced by a German company. It is part of our Empire brand, which has passed €1 billion in revenue and 220 million registered players. Now we are moving the game from Adobe AIR to Unity. Quality is the heart of that move: the Unity client has to behave exactly like today’s client, 1:1, including its known quirks, while the live team keeps shipping new content every month.

We are looking for a QA Automation Engineer, Mobile Games - Freelance who builds that proof as an automated, AI-assisted test setup: automation first, AI agents for the legwork, people for the judgement calls, and no endless manual passes.

This is a senior freelance role where you work autonomously, full-time from February 2027 until the end of 2027 including handover. It is fully remote within ±3 hours of CET, with the option to meet as a team in one of our Hamburg offices.

YOUR MISSION

  • Design the test strategy and test plans for the port based on the live game, game design documents and the list of features to migrate. Prioritise by risk and agree the standards with the game’s QA lead.

  • Build automated tests that run the AIR client and the Unity client side by side: same input, same result. Think replayed server traffic, state comparison and pixel diffs, where pass or fail is deterministic, not a judgement call.

  • Use AI tools like Claude as a real part of your work: to generate and maintain test scripts, explore the game, cluster crashes and draft bug reports, with a human checking the result. Build tooling where it pays off, and measure whether it does.

  • Perform smoke tests, sanity checks and full regression testing for every port build, and turn each new live feature and content release into regression cases for the Unity client.

  • Test what players feel: payments and in-app purchases, store builds, login, push notifications, localisation, and the analytics events the business relies on, checked event by event with the data team.

  • Run a device matrix on real devices, including low-end Android phones and older iPhones, and track load time, memory, frame rate, heat and battery against the live client.

  • Identify, document and report defects in Jira, manage tickets and coordinate with the port team so that release deadlines are met.

  • Support the release in a first market and then on all stores: release candidates, store certification, a tested rollback path and clear go or no-go input.

  • Hand over a test suite and documentation that the live QA team can run and extend after the port.

WHO YOU’LL WORK WITH

You join the port team of Empire: Four Kingdoms and report to the project lead.

  • Project lead: the owner of the port, who sets priorities and is your day-to-day contact.

  • The game’s QA lead: reviews your test approach and signs off quality for the Empire team.

  • The port team: the Lead Unity Engineer, the Unity developers and a second QA Engineer joining later. You share test plans, review each other’s work and keep one testing standard.

  • The Empire team: producers, game designers, client and server developers who know the game inside out. You involve them early and learn from them.

  • Data team: to check that the tracking events from the Unity client mean the same as today.

  • External QA partners: where we use them, you help coordinate their testing.

YOUR BACKSTORY

  • 6+ years of hands-on QA experience in games, with a focus on test automation and a solid understanding of the bug life cycle and testing methodologies.

  • You have tested at least one live mobile game with a significant user base, through store release and live updates. This is a hard requirement.

  • Hands-on mobile and game test automation, for example Appium, AltTester, GameDriver, Unity Test Framework or comparable tools, and scripting in Python, C# or a similar language, including running tests in CI.

  • You work autonomously: you own your test approach, set priorities with the project lead and raise risks early, without needing day-to-day direction.

  • Practical experience using AI tools (Claude, Cursor, Copilot or similar) in QA: generating and maintaining tests, triaging failures, writing tooling. You know where they help and where they don’t.

jobs.title: Senior Manager Operations and Allocations
jobs.description:
Position overview
SNV is building a commercial markets accelerator, built to close the gap between capital and impact where both are urgently needed. This is a lean unit with a single P&L, a break-even mandate, and a team that spans two revenue streams, multiple geographies, and a mix of hires and consultants. The Senior Manager for Operations and Allocations is the engine room. This person owns the financial backbone of the Accelerator, keeps a constant eye on profitability and spend, manages how team members and partners are allocated across assignments, and ensures the internal systems and processes work well enough to create commercial speed rather than administrative drag.

The right profile is someone with the financial rigour of a management accountant, the operational instincts of a COO, and the interpersonal skills to manage resource conversations in a small, fast-moving team where everyone has competing priorities. This is not a support function. It is a strategic role that directly determines whether the Accelerator reaches break-even.

Who you are
You are a commercially minded operations leader who thrives in building and scaling new ventures. You combine strong financial and analytical skills with the ability to design practical operating models, processes, and systems that enable teams to perform at their best.

You are naturally curious and challenge the status quo. Rather than accepting existing processes as given, you assess whether they are fit for purpose and look for opportunities to improve efficiency, decision-making, and client experience. You bring an external, commercially focused perspective and are comfortable questioning established ways of working when a better approach exists.

You are equally comfortable working with numbers, people, and systems. You understand the financial drivers of a business and can translate financial insights into operational decisions that improve profitability, resource utilization, and performance. At the same time, you build strong relationships, navigate competing priorities, and influence stakeholders with confidence and credibility.

You enjoy operating in ambiguity and are energized by creating structure where little exists. You take ownership, work independently, and proactively identify opportunities to improve how work gets done. As a trusted partner to senior leadership, you help shift operational responsibilities away from others by bringing sound judgement, practical solutions, and a strong bias for action.

Most importantly, you are motivated by building something new. You have the mindset of a problem solver, the rigor of a financial operator, and the confidence to create systems and ways of working that allow a fast-growing commercial venture to deliver impact at speed and scale.

Key Responsibilities

Financial management

  • Own the Accelerator's P&L — monthly tracking of revenue, costs, and contribution margin by stream and by engagement.
  • Maintain actuals vs forecast on a rolling basis. Flag variances to the Director within the week they emerge.
  • Manage invoicing: raise invoices on time, track payments, chase overdue receivables.
  • Negotiate and manage consultant and sub-contractor contracts — day rates, scope, payment milestones.
  • Prepare the quarterly financial report for the steering committee.
  • Own the budget reallocation process — track what has been spent, what remains, and flag when lines are at risk of overrun before they overrun.
  • Support the Director on financial inputs to stage gate dossiers. You will own a significant portion of each dossier: P&L actuals, budget variance, headcount status, and pipeline financial summary. This is not a supporting role on stage gates — it is a delivery role.

Resource allocation

  • Maintain a live allocation view: who is on what engagement, at what percentage, and through to when.
  • Identify capacity constraints before they become delivery problems — flag to the Director when team members are overcommitted.
  • Manage the transition of team members between engagements: close-out on one, mobilisation on the next.
  • Coordinate with the Director and stream leads on consultant sourcing when engagements require specialist inputs the core team cannot cover.
  • Track billable time across the team — ensuring the right proportion of staff time is recoverable against client engagements. Own the time-tracking system: select, set up, and maintain the tool. Billability data is only as good as the data behind it.

Partner and sub-contractor network

  • Own the onboarding process for consultants and sub-contractors: vetting, due diligence, SNV compliance checks, contract execution.
  • Maintain a curated roster of preferred partners by specialism and geography — available and pre-qualified when an engagement needs them. Framework agreements with preferred partners are the default contracting model: commercial terms, liability, and quality standards agreed in advance so the unit can issue call-offs rather than negotiate from scratch on every bid.
  • Own the internal sub-contracting mechanism with other SNV teams: budget transfer process, accountability structure, quality standards, and escalation path.
  • Manage ongoing partner relationships: performance tracking, rate reviews, framework agreement renewals.
  • Build new partner relationships proactively — particularly in geographies or technical areas where the Accelerator's coverage is thin.

Internal systems and operations

  • Own the CRM — ensure it is live, accurate, and used. The pipeline data is only as good as the discipline behind it.
  • Maintain operating systems: project management tools, document management, reporting templates. Resolve the IT boundary question with SNV ICT: establish which tools sit inside SNV’s environment and which do not, and under what governance conditions.
  • Own the data governance framework: who owns data in each system, who has access, what categories of information can be processed through AI tools, and what must remain within SNV’s controlled environment.
  • Run the monthly internal review: pipeline status, allocation, financials. Prepare the materials; run the meeting.
  • Manage ongoing compliance requirements — procurement processes, finance reporting, HR administration.
  • Identify and flag any internal process that is creating drag on the team's commercial activity. Propose and implement fixes.

What you bring

To be considered for this role, you bring:

  • At least 8 years in operations, finance, or management roles — with direct experience managing a P&L or project budget in a commercial or consulting context.
  • Experience in resource allocation or capacity planning in a professional services or consulting environment.
  • Track record of managing consultant or sub-contractor networks — sourcing, contracting, and performance management.
  • Experience working in or with development organisations, international NGOs, or similar — familiarity with donor compliance, reporting requirements, and the operational constraints of internationally dispersed teams.
  • Experience building and running internal operating systems from scratch, not just inheriting and maintaining them.
  • Experience establishing or managing framework agreements with external suppliers or delivery partners.

Additionally, we value:

  • Strong financial management skills — comfortable with P&L tracking, margin analysis, and budget forecasting.
  • Proficiency with CRM tools, project management software, and financial tracking systems.
  • Exceptional organisational skills. You track many things simultaneously without dropping any.
  • Good negotiator — with consultants, with suppliers, and internally when competing priorities need to be resolved.
  • Comfortable evaluating and selecting operational tools — CRM, time tracking, project management, pipeline management. You can assess options against the team’s actual workflow rather than defaulting to what is already available.
  • English required. French or Portuguese an advantage.
  • Reporting line: Director
  • Location: Flexible.We welcome applications from candidates based anywhere within the time zones spanning Ghana to Singapore. As this role involves international collaboration and travel, candidates should be located within reasonable reach of a well-connected international airport.
  • Travel requirements: International travel will be required.
  • Expected start date: January 2027

What we offer
We offer a competitive salary and benefits package. Compensation is determined based on relevant experience, skills, and internal equity, ensuring a fair and consistent approach across the organisation.

Location & Travel
Flexible location. We are particularly interested in candidates based within the time zones between Singapore and Ghana, where most of our work is concentrated. International travel will be required, so candidates should have access to a major international airport.

Contract duration: We are looking for someone to play a long-term role in building and growing the Accelerator. Contract arrangements will vary by location and local employment requirements, and details will be discussed with shortlisted candidates.

Working at SNV
At SNV we challenge and inspire and offer continuous growth. We offer meaningful opportunities to shape the future, expand your skills, and collaborate with a vibrant, global network of experts. At SNV your contribution matter, and your development is our priority.

We are home to 57 cultures working in 22 countries, with about 95% of our team members holding the nationality of the respective countries we work in. We promote international career development. Our workforce consists of a mix of both people with longstanding tenure, willing to share their institutional knowledge, as well as people with local expertise and knowledge. All with an inquisitive view and united in ‘ONE SNV’ working towards our purpose.

Together, we are committed to the effective and efficient stewardship of resources and maximising positive, lasting impacts. Our ability to deliver results rests on our robust foundation of experience, technical knowledge, evidence and learning; our commitment to strengthening capacities and catalysing partnerships; and the relationships and trust of those we work alongside.

SNV is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse work environment and make recruitment decisions based on merit, competence, and organisational needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, nationality, marital status, or any other status protected by applicable law. Women, persons with disabilities, and candidates from under-represented backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.

How to apply
If you meet the key requirements and feel inspired by this opportunity, we warmly welcome your application. Please submit your CV and motivation letter by 15th of December 2026 via SmartRecruiters.

To ensure a focused and respectful recruitment process, we kindly ask that you apply only if you meet the essential qualifications and are available to work in the specified location.
Please note that only candidates progressing to the next stage of the selection process will be contacted. Individual feedback cannot be provided.

If this role isn’t the right fit but you’re interested in joining SNV in the future, we invite you to follow us on LinkedIn and our career page Vacancies | SNV to stay updated on new opportunities that match your profile.

Reference and vetting check
At SNV, our belief in the CARE principles — Commitment to impact, Adaptive to Context, Respecting Difference and Expertise in Practice — shapes how we work with each other and every interaction we have with our colleagues, partners, and the communities we serve. These values guide how we welcome new team members, ensuring our workplace remains a place of trust, safety, and dignity for all.

As part of our commitment to a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, we carry out reference and background checks for all determined positions, with particular attention to safeguarding. You will be invited to provide the contact details of [two] referees, and we will only approach them once you have given your permission. We handle this process with care, empathy, and strict confidentiality, using the information solely for purposes related to your application and the role you have applied for.

SNV is committed to safeguarding and to protecting children and adults from all forms of harm, with zero tolerance for sexual exploitation, abuse, harassment, or any other form of misconduct. As part of creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive working environment, all staff, consultants, and partners are expected to uphold SNV’s safeguarding, child protection, ethical standards, and CARE principles. In line with these commitments — and as a participant in the Inter‑Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS) — SNV will request a Statement of Conduct from your previous employer(s), covering any substantiated findings of misconduct, to ensure a recruitment process that safeguards and protect the communities we serve.

About SNV Proximate
What if you could combine the commercial rigour of consulting, investment, or corporate strategy with the opportunity to create meaningful development impact at scale? SNV’s newly established impact capital accelerator aims to do exactly that: develop commercially viable solutions that generate both business value and development impact. Combining expertise in impact-driven finance and inclusive commercial value chains, SNV Proximate will operate with the pace, ambition, and commercial mindset of a boutique advisory firm while leveraging the reach, credibility, and market presence of a global development organisation.

Working with companies, investors, development finance institutions, foundations, and governments, this is your chance to join the team that will design, test, and grow new approaches to mobilising investment, strengthening markets, and building more inclusive and resilient value chains across emerging economies. It is a place for people who are excited by building something new, comfortable operating across both commercial and development environments, and motivated by turning ambitious ideas into scalable results.

jobs.title: Security Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) Manager
jobs.description:
We are hiring a Security Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) Manager to lead the team that keeps Canonical's security and compliance credible to the Enterprises, Clouds, Telcos and Governments that run on Ubuntu, and to bring our controls and risk management to the standard a public company requires.

Location: EMEA or Americas — fully remote (home-based), with the option to work from our London office.

About our Team

Canonical's customers trust Ubuntu with critical systems. That trust rests on evidence: our ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certifications, how we manage risk, and how we respond as security regulation such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act reaches open source software. The Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) team produces that evidence and makes it real across the company. As Canonical prepares to list on a public exchange, the team is also central to the controls and risk reporting our Audit Committee and Board rely on.

The team is part of Operations and reports to the Chief Operating Officer. It covers both sides of the discipline: keeping us certified and compliant today, and looking ahead at risk across corporate IT, infrastructure and products. It works closely with Engineering, Security Operations, Information Systems, Legal, Finance and Sales.

You will lead the team, set its priorities and operating rhythm, and be the first escalation point for security and compliance decisions.

What you'll do

  • Lead and develop a team of GRC engineers: hire, coach and set priorities, and run a roadmap that balances planned work with operational requests, so the team delivers predictably and reports progress clearly to leadership. You own the team’s budget, vendors and tooling.
  • Own our ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certifications end to end: audit readiness, evidence collection, auditor relationships and fieldwork, so certifications are renewed on time with clean outcomes.
  • Run the risk management framework across corporate IT, infrastructure and products — asset classification, risk assessments, the risk register and key risk indicators — so leadership and the Board can see and decide on the company’s most important risks.
  • Own the information security policy framework — annual reviews, new policies, exceptions and risk acceptance — and make the call, or escalate it, when a policy and a business need conflict.
  • Partner with Finance on IT General Controls and internal controls over financial reporting — remediation, control execution and Audit Committee reporting — to make Canonical ready for a public listing.
  • Turn security regulation and standards — the EU Cyber Resilience Act, NIS2, DORA, the EU AI Act and IEC 62443 — into practical programmes with Legal and Engineering, including our secure software development lifecycle and penetration testing, so our products meet their obligations as they ship.
  • Build business continuity and disaster recovery with Information Systems and business owners — impact analysis, plans and tested recovery — so critical services can be restored when it matters.
  • Oversee third-party risk, access reviews and the governance of new tools and AI usage, and support customers and colleagues when it counts — security questionnaires, RFPs, our Trust Center, contract security terms and incident response — alongside Sales, Legal and Security Operations.

What we are looking for in you

  • Hands-on ownership of ISO 27001 and/or SOC 2 certification through external audit cycles
  • Experience designing or running a risk management framework (such as ISO 27005, NIST CSF or ISO 31000), including a risk register and reporting to senior leadership
  • Experience with IT General Controls supporting financial audits, under SOX or an equivalent regime
  • Experience leading a governance, risk and compliance, security compliance or IT risk team in a software or technology company
  • Experience turning regulatory and technical requirements into controls that engineering and business teams you don’t manage actually adopt
  • Sound judgement on risk acceptance and policy exceptions, and the confidence to hold a position with senior stakeholders
  • Passion for technology evidenced by personal projects and initiatives
  • Exceptional academic track record from both high school and university
  • Professional written and spoken English with excellent presentation skills
  • Ability to travel internationally twice a year for company events up to two weeks long

Nice-to-have skills

  • Experience preparing a company for a public listing
  • Experience with product security compliance for a software vendor (EU Cyber Resilience Act, IEC 62443 or NIST SSDF)
  • Business continuity and disaster recovery programme experience
  • Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA or ISO 27001 Lead Auditor or Lead Implementer

How we work

We look for a track record of going above-and-beyond expectations to achieve outstanding results, backed by self-motivation and drive. Our people deliver their work precisely, taking care to deliver correctness and clarity. Reliability is at our core, where colleagues deliver high quality work that builds trust and confidence. We make ourselves accessible, collaborating to build products and systems that are usable. Finally we are adroit, blending enthusiasm, knowledge, adaptability, style and character.

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment, with bi-annual team travel to connect in person
  • Priority Pass for travel
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Bi-annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination, and regardless of your identity we will give your application fair consideration.

jobs.title: Connected Devices - Solution Implementation Lead
jobs.description:
Job Title: Connected Devices - Solution Implementation Lead

Job Location: London, Greater London, United Kingdom

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

The Solution Implementation Lead is the end‑to‑end execution owner and subject‑matter expert for the development, validation, and operationalization of new connected medical device and digital health solutions.

This role partners closely with the Strategic Solutions Lead to evaluate, shape, and deliver new solution offerings aligned to the strategic priorities of the Connected Devices business, with a primary focus on the respiratory service line. The role bridges strategy, execution, validation, and operational readiness, ensuring solutions progress from concept through Business Go‑Live and are ready for scalable study deployment.

Key Responsibilities and Oversight

Experience supporting respiratory clinical trials (e.g., asthma, COPD, pulmonary indications) is required. Candidates without direct respiratory trial experience clearly demonstrated within their resume will not be considered.

Solution Evaluation & Strategy Support

  • Partner with Strategic Solutions Leads (SSL) to evaluate new digital health and medical device solutions aligned to Connected Devices strategy.
  • Provide SME input into solution feasibility, operational workflows, regulatory considerations, and validation approach.
  • Support Strategic Solutions as needed with business case development, budget inputs, go-to-market strategy and customer-facing SME in customer presentations.

End‑to‑End Solution Startup Execution Ownership

  • Own end‑to‑end execution of approved solutions from business case approval through Business Go‑Live, serving as the single point of accountability for startup outcomes.
  • Develop and manage the startup plan, including milestones, dependencies, risks, constraints, and mitigation strategies.
  • Ensure solution design, operational workflows, and validation activities are aligned with study, program, and stakeholder needs.
  • Confirm readiness at each startup stage and before Business Go‑Live.

Cross‑Functional Orchestration & Technical Leadership

  • Lead and coordinate execution across Engineering, IT, Validation, QA, Regulatory, Data Management, Operations, Logistics, Vendors, Field Support and Training.
  • Translate high‑level solution concepts into clear device, system, service, and validation requirements understood by technical and validation teams.
  • Support vendor relationships, including issue resolution, design alignment, and budget collaboration.
  • Provide expert troubleshooting guidance to operations and support teams; engage with sites and customers as needed to resolve complex issues.

Solution‑Level Readiness, Quality & Compliance

  • Ensure solution‑level readiness, including documentation, validation completion, training delivery, support models, and escalation pathways.
  • Partner closely with Solution Specialists to ensure regulatory and compliance requirements are met without late‑stage disruption.
  • Lead quality management, process improvement, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Contribute to internal SOPs, study templates, and site/patient‑facing materials as a solution SME.

Governance, Escalation & Stakeholder Management Oversight

  • Own resolution of startup‑level issues; escalate appropriately when:
  • Scope or solution intent is impacted (to Strategic Solutions Lead)
  • Timeline, investment, or delivery risk requires acceptance (to Governance / Sponsor)
  • Provide clear, consistent communications to internal stakeholders, sponsors, and leadership on startup status, risks, and readiness.
  • Transfer ownership at Business Go‑Live to study execution leadership (e.g., CD Project Manager) and retain an escalation/support role for solution‑level issues post‑handoff.

Required Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Strong knowledge of digital health, connected medical devices, and regulated clinical environments is required and must be clearly outlined in your resume/CV.
  • Working knowledge of FDA guidelines and global regulatory expectations and their operational impact.
  • Advanced project and program management skills in complex, matrixed organizations.
  • Excellent technical aptitude related to systems, platforms, integrations, and device workflows.
  • Strong communication, stakeholder management, and executive‑level presentation skills.
  • Proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal teams, vendors, sponsors, sites, and clients.
  • Occasional travel may be required.

Minimum Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
  • 10+ years of relevant experience in healthcare, pharmaceutical, life sciences, or digital health environments.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience managing people, operations, and cross‑functional initiatives.
  • Strong business acumen with experience supporting solution development, commercialization, and delivery.

This is a remote opportunity open to candidates currently residing in EMEA.

IQVIA is a leading global provider of clinical research services, commercial insights and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences and healthcare industries. We create intelligent connections to accelerate the development and commercialization of innovative medical treatments to help improve patient outcomes and population health worldwide. Learn more at

IQVIA is committed to integrity in our hiring process and maintains a zero tolerance policy for candidate fraud. All information and credentials submitted in your application must be truthful and complete. Any false statements, misrepresentations, or material omissions during the recruitment process will result in immediate disqualification of your application, or termination of employment if discovered later, in accordance with applicable law. We appreciate your honesty and professionalism.

jobs.title: Solutions Engineer EMEA - Remote (Contract to Hire)
jobs.description:
About DigiStor

DigiStor develops secure data-at-rest solutions for enterprise, government, defense, and other security-conscious organizations. Our portfolio includes secure and self-encrypting SSDs, removable NVMe storage solutions, and technologies designed for demanding client, workstation, server, and edge environments.

Role Overview

The Field Engineer, EMEA will be DigiStor's primary customer-facing technical resource supporting two EMEA Sales Representatives.

The role combines technical pre-sales, solution design, product demonstrations, platform qualification, and field support. You will help customers select, evaluate, integrate, and deploy DigiStor secure-storage solutions within Dell Technologies and HP/HPE client, workstation, server, and edge platforms.

You will work closely with customers, channel partners, OEM contacts, Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Testing, and Technical Support. Your purpose will be to remove technical barriers, reduce risk, and help convert qualified opportunities into successful deployments.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Pre-Sales

  • Partner with two EMEA Sales Representatives throughout the customer engagement lifecycle.
  • Lead technical discovery sessions to understand the customer's platform, workload, security, performance, environmental, and compliance requirements.
  • Recommend the most appropriate DigiStor product, capacity, form factor, interface, and security configuration.
  • Translate complex storage and security concepts into clear business and operational benefits.
  • Deliver technical presentations, product demonstrations, workshops, and architecture discussions.
  • Support customer responses, proposals, RFIs, RFPs, technical questionnaires, and tender submissions.
  • Help Sales identify technical risks, dependencies, and qualification requirements early in the opportunity.

Platform and Solution Engineering

  • Advise customers on the integration of DigiStor solutions into Dell and HP/HPE servers, workstations, desktops, laptops, and edge platforms.
  • Assess compatibility across NVMe, SATA, PCIe, BIOS/UEFI, operating systems, firmware, physical form factors, power, cooling, and thermal requirements.
  • Support storage technologies and form factors including M.2, U.2, U.3, E1.S, SATA, and removable NVMe solutions.
  • Develop recommended configurations, compatibility guidance, bills of material, and solution documentation.
  • Work with DigiStor Engineering and Testing teams to coordinate platform validation and resolve compatibility questions.

Evaluations and Proofs of Concept

  • Define and manage customer evaluations, proof-of-concept activities, and product qualification plans.
  • Establish clear technical success criteria with customers and Sales.
  • Assist with product installation, configuration, testing, benchmarking, and results interpretation.
  • Capture diagnostic information, reproduce reported issues where possible, and coordinate escalation to the appropriate Engineering or Support team.
  • Maintain ownership and clear customer communication through technical resolution and handover.

Secure-Storage Expertise

  • Explain secure-storage technologies including hardware encryption, self-encrypting drives, TCG Opal, pre-boot authentication, key management, and secure erase.
  • Help customers understand relevant certification and compliance requirements, including FIPS, Common Criteria, TAA, NATO, and regional security programmes.
  • Ensure that technical claims and recommendations accurately reflect product capabilities and certification status.
  • Support customers operating in regulated, government, defence, financial-services, healthcare, and critical-infrastructure environments.

Partner and Field Enablement

  • Develop strong technical relationships with customers, distributors, resellers, integrators, and OEM stakeholders across EMEA.
  • Deliver technical training and enablement sessions for channel and sales partners.
  • Create and maintain technical guides, configuration notes, FAQs, reference architectures, and field playbooks.
  • Bring structured customer feedback, competitive intelligence, and emerging requirements back to DigiStor's Product and Engineering teams.
  • Represent DigiStor at customer meetings, partner events, industry events, and technical briefings.

Required Experience and Knowledge

  • Proven experience as a Field Engineer, Sales Engineer, Systems Engineer, Solutions Architect, Field Applications Engineer, or Technical Pre-Sales Engineer.
  • Strong working knowledge of Dell Technologies and HP/HPE client, workstation, and server platforms.
  • Practical understanding of enterprise storage, SSDs, NVMe, SATA, PCIe, firmware, BIOS/UEFI, and storage-device integration.
  • Experience supporting both Windows and Linux environments.
  • Ability to diagnose hardware, firmware, operating-system, performance, and compatibility issues.
  • Experience planning and delivering customer evaluations or proofs of concept.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with infrastructure architects, security teams, IT operations, procurement teams, partners, and senior decision-makers.
  • Strong written and spoken English.
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly across EMEA.
  • Ability to work independently within a geographically distributed organisation.

Desirable Experience

  • Knowledge of self-encrypting drives, TCG Opal, AES-256 encryption, pre-boot authentication, and data-at-rest security.
  • Familiarity with FIPS 140-2/140-3, Common Criteria, CSfC, TAA, NATO, UK, or European security requirements.
  • Experience with Dell OEM, HP/HPE, or other major hardware-manufacturer ecosystems.
  • Experience with storage-testing and diagnostic tools such as NVMe CLI, SMART utilities, fio, Iometer, and operating-system hardware tools.
  • Experience supporting government, defence, financial-services, healthcare, industrial, or other regulated customers.
  • Knowledge of removable storage, rugged systems, edge computing, or industrial computing environments.
  • Fluency in an additional European language.

Core Competencies

  • Support beneficiary feedback mechanisms and work with partners to ensure patient and community feedback is addressed appropriately.
  • Represent Smile Train locally and support awareness, advocacy, content collection, patient and partner stories, events, donor or auditor visits, and brand-compliant communications.
  • Strengthen relationships with relevant external stakeholders and advocate for sustainable, safe, high-quality, comprehensive cleft care, including the inclusion of cleft care in national health priorities where appropriate.

Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a proactive, culturally sensitive program professional with strong partner management skills, sound judgment, and a commitment to high-quality, safe, patient-centered cleft care.   • Bachelor’s degree in public health, Social Sciences, International Relations, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of relevant experience in program coordination or management, preferably in public health, global health, development, or nonprofit programming.

  • Strong computer literacy, including Microsoft Office and the ability to navigate databases, dashboards, and datasets.
  • Fluency in English and Arabic is required; strong written and verbal communication skills are essential.
  • Good understanding of the local context in Egypt, including cultural dynamics and challenges affecting access to services in underserved communities.
  • Must be based in Egypt and willing to travel frequently to partner sites, events, and remote locations as required.

Additional Eligibility Qualifications

  • Ability to work effectively with a global team across time zones and cultures.
  • Non-Profit experience preferred.
  • Strong time management, organizational, problem-solving, and follow-through skills.
  • Ability to work independently with appropriate supervision, initiative, confidentiality, and accountability.
  • Preference for candidates based in Cairo.

Compensation

$ 27,000 - 30,000 USD Annually

Travel

This is a full-time role. Significant travel is expected to partner locations, events, and field sites within Egypt, including travel to remote or underserved areas as needed.

Why You’ll Love Working Here!

Smile Train offers a range of innovative benefits...

  • Meaningful Work – Be part of work that creates meaningful, lasting impact — changing the world one smile at a time.
  • We’ve Got You Covered – Enjoy a generous stipend towards medical expenses to help prioritize the health of you and your family.
  • Rest and Recharge - Enjoy a generous vacation package, paid holidays, and sick time so you can rest, recharge, and return feeling your best.

  • Learn and Grow - Take advantage of an annual professional development stipend and opportunities to expand your skills and continue learning.
  • Work Your Way – Thrive with a remote work model built for connection, balance, and impact.
  • Travel the World – See our impact firsthand while partnering with global colleagues and programs through opportunities for domestic and international trave

Accountability Expectations

  • Emotional Intelligence: Demonstrate empathy, understanding, and cultural sensitivity to contribute to an inclusive and supportive team environment.
  • Empowerment: Effectively communicate with supervisors to ensure you are equipped with the resources, guidance, and autonomy you need to excel in your role.
  • Team Cohesion: Contribute to a culture of collaboration, mutual respect, and shared accountability, helping the team to thrive in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

Application Process

Smile Train is an equal opportunity employer, committed to inclusive hiring and dedicated to diversity in our work and staff. We strongly encourage candidates from all groups and communities to apply.

jobs.title: Senior Compliance Manager, Derivatives Trade Reporting
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Opportunity

OKX is hiring a Senior Compliance Officer to build and run our global derivatives trade and transaction reporting function. The function covers CFTC swap data reporting under Part 45, EU transaction reporting under MiFIR, EU derivatives reporting under EMIR, UK MiFIR and UK EMIR, and ASIC derivative transaction reporting across multiple OKX entities and a growing derivatives product set. These regimes have different scopes, reporting parties, data requirements and destinations. You will determine how they apply to OKX’s activities and help build a reliable process for meeting each obligation.
Most of the work is data and judgment: deciding what is reportable, by which entity, and to whom, then making sure the right trade and lifecycle data reaches the right swap data repository, trade repository, or regulator on time and reconciles to our trading records. You will own reporting scoping/eligibility, submission monitoring, and the controls that show our reports are complete, accurate, and timely.
This is a hands-on Compliance leadership role. You will work with Trading, Product, Engineering, Data, Legal, local Compliance teams and reporting providers, and you will lead regulatory change in this space. Responsibilities for source data, systems, submissions and remediation will be agreed across those teams; you will lead the compliance framework and stay close enough to the process to identify and proactively resolve problems. You will report to the Head of Markets and Product Compliance and support a central function that owns reporting interpretation, scoping, oversight, and remediation for every entity in scope.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Interpret and apply derivatives and transaction reporting rules across global regimes, including CFTC Part 45, MiFIR Article 26, EMIR Article 9, UK MiFIR, UK EMIR, and the ASIC Derivative Transaction Rules (Reporting) 2024, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and outside counsel.
  • Own and maintain entity, product, and transaction-level reporting scoping and eligibility: which entity reports, which products and lifecycle events are in scope, which counterparty role triggers the obligation, and which repository or authority receives the report.
  • Oversee, support, and help maintain the daily reporting process. Monitor submissions against deadlines, including T+1 for MiFIR transaction reports, investigate rejections and breaks, and track each one to resolution.
  • Reconcile reported activity to trading records and repository data, and coordinate corrections and back-reporting with the teams that own the relevant systems and data.
  • Define and maintain the reporting data specification with Engineering and Data, including field-level mapping, reference data such as LEIs, UTIs, UPIs, and ISINs, and the validation rules applied before submission.
  • Build and run the control framework: completeness, accuracy, and timeliness checks, exception management, management information, and records that hold up to regulator and audit review.
  • Drive reporting readiness and remediation. Assess new derivatives products, new entities, and regulatory changes, identify control gaps, agree on owners and deadlines across Compliance, Operations, Product, and Engineering, and track delivery.
  • Escalate material issues. Assess the impact of reporting errors, escalate to senior management, and support notifications to regulators where required.
  • Manage relationships with swap data repositories, trade repositories, approved reporting mechanisms, and reporting vendors, including onboarding, testing, and service issues.
  • Hands-on leader. Build a small team, and coordinate with and train local compliance leads.
  • Support independent testing by Compliance Monitoring, Risk, and Internal Audit, and support regulator inquiries with complete, reproducible records.

What We Look For In You

  • A degree in finance, economics, law, data science, or computer science, or an equivalent professional qualification
  • 7+ years in trade reporting, transaction reporting, or regulatory reporting at an exchange, broker, bank, trading firm, fintech, or digital asset platform
  • Deep working knowledge of at least two of the following regimes: CFTC swap data reporting, MiFIR transaction reporting, EMIR, UK MiFIR, UK EMIR, and ASIC derivative transaction reporting. Hands-on experience with both a US and a European regime is strongly preferred.
  • A sound understanding of derivatives trade lifecycles and the data needed to report executions, changes, terminations and, where applicable, valuations and collateral.
  • The ability to interrogate large datasets, investigate reporting breaks and explain clear requirements to engineers and other business partners. SQL or comparable data analysis skills are highly desirable.
  • Experience building or improving a reporting framework, including procedures, reconciliations, exception management and evidence that can withstand regulatory or audit scrutiny; this may include remediating historical reporting errors, including back-reporting.
  • The judgment to make proportionate risk decisions, escalate material issues and lead delivery across teams without relying on a single team to own every part of the reporting process.
  • Experience with digital asset derivatives, such as perpetual futures and options, and how they map to reporting product classifications

Nice to Haves

  • Experience leading a regulatory reporting change program, such as EMIR Refit, UK EMIR Refit, the CFTC reporting rewrite, or the ASIC 2024 rules.
  • Familiarity with ISO 20022 XML reporting formats.
  • Python or similar scripting for data validation, and experience with data warehouse tools such as Databricks.

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company events
  • More that we love to tell you along the process!
