Today, these areas work differently from one product to the next. Processes, tools and standards vary in many cases, and too much depends on a few people who know a product or a platform inside out. We want one modern, professional operation that runs around the clock and that customers experience the same way, whichever product they use and wherever/however it is deployed.

We are looking for someone to build this team and lead it. You will set the operating model, lead the three teams, own escalations through to resolution, and put the tooling, processes and measures in place to run Service Operations as a true 24/7 managed service. You will sit on the COO’s leadership team and take on wider operational responsibility as the function matures. It is a senior leadership role, but you will need to stay close enough to the work to know what good looks like and to step in when it counts.

WHY THIS ROLE

This is a new function with a direct line to the COO. You will shape it from the start, with real backing to change how we work and a clear mandate to build a professional service that customers value. It is also a role with room to grow: as the function matures, we expect you to take on wider operational responsibility across the business.

The role is remote and the location is open. Because Service Operations runs 24/7, you will take part in senior escalation cover for major incidents, and potentially travel occasionally to meet the team and customers.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Team Leadership & People Management

  • Lead the three teams that report to you, specifically, Level 1 Support, Hosting Support and Infrastructure Management, and build and retain Level 2 knowledge over time.
  • Build out the Level 1 team, starting with a new team being established, and make sure it works hand in hand with our existing product support specialists in the Cincom business.
  • Hire, develop and coach the team, and cross-skill people across products and platforms so we are not reliant on any one person.
  • Set clear objectives, give regular feedback, and build a team that takes ownership of the customer’s problem.

Operational Leadership

  • Sit on the COO’s leadership team and contribute to decisions across engineering, delivery and operations.
  • Deputise for the COO on operational matters when needed, and take on wider operational responsibility as the function matures.
  • Own the Service Operations budget, including hosting and infrastructure costs, and help deliver against the business’s cost and efficiency targets.
  • Manage key operational suppliers and contracts, working with the COO and PartnerOne Group procurement and IT where Group agreements apply.

Building a 24/7 Service Operations Function

  • Design and run Service Operations as a true 24/7 service, with coverage, rotas and on-call arrangements that match our customer commitments.
  • Build out-of-hours models that make good use of the team, without burning people out.
  • Replace product-by-product ways of working with one consistent model for intake, triage, severity and prioritisation.
  • Bring in modern support practice, including ITIL-aligned incident, problem and change management and knowledge-centred support.
  • Build a proper Managed Services approach for our hosted platforms, working across the Hosting Support and Infrastructure teams and with the Client Success Team for our key accounts.

Escalation Management to Level 2 and 3

  • Own the escalation process from Level 1 into Level 2/3: product engineering teams for product issues, and Services consultants for issues in project deliverables, where necessary.
  • Set clear criteria for when and how issues escalate, so they arrive with the right information, and nothing gets lost in the handover.
  • Track every escalated issue through to resolution, keep customers informed, chase when timescales slip.
  • Review escalation trends with the product heads, push recurring issues back for permanent fixes and inclusion in roadmaps and make sure what we learn is captured in the smart knowledge base.

Hosting Support

  • Hold overall accountability for the customer environments Cincom hosts and manages, delivered through the Hosting Support team, and stay engaged with customer hosted deployments and associated metrics.
  • Make sure hosted services meet their commitments on availability, monitoring, backups, patching, disaster recovery and incident response, around the clock, providing a true Managed Service.
  • Turn hosting into a consistent, repeatable managed service that our commercial team can understand and sell with confidence.

Infrastructure

  • Lead the Infrastructure team and own the hardware and deployment design for hosted and on-premise customer environments. Software design stays with the product engineering teams.
  • Set infrastructure standards and reference architectures for each product, covering capacity, resilience, security and cost.
  • Plan capacity and sizing with the product and project delivery teams, so customer environments are built right first time.
  • Keep our cloud and infrastructure estate, including Azure and Kubernetes, secure, patched, documented and cost-effective.

Tooling, Automation & AI

  • Make Zoho Desk the single platform for support, configured properly and used consistently across every product, with integrations into other Cincom operational platforms as required.
  • Build and maintain a knowledge base (working with Cincom designated AI tools) that customers and the team actually use and expand self-service and automation where it saves everyone effort.
  • Work with our AI team to explore and develop AI-assisted Level 1 support, including local-language support, with validation before answers reach customers.

Performance, Reporting & Compliance

  • Set and track SLAs and internal service levels for response and resolution, by severity.
  • Report on ticket trends by product, customer, region, severity and SLA tracked resolution time, alongside hosting availability and infrastructure cost, not just ticket status, and review them monthly with the COO.
  • Lead the response to major incidents, with clear and timely communication to customers following a well-documented process.
  • Make sure support, hosting and infrastructure processes provide the evidence we need for ISO 27001 and SOC 2, and support our obligations to customers in regulated sectors.

Requirements

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Essential Experience

  • Experience leading support, hosting or infrastructure operations for enterprise software customers, ideally across more than one product.
  • Experience leading several teams through team leads, at senior management level.
  • A track record of building or reshaping a support or operations function, not only running an existing one.
  • Experience running or building a 24/7 support operation, including on-call and potential follow-the-sun models.
  • Experience managing escalations into engineering teams and holding them to agreed timescales.
  • Experience running SLA-based support for business-critical customer systems.
  • Experience owning an operational budget, including hosting and infrastructure costs.

Technical Knowledge

  • Strong grounding in incident, problem and change management (ITIL or equivalent).
  • Solid understanding of hosted and cloud infrastructure, Azure or similar, including monitoring and alerting, high availability, backup and disaster recovery, and management of guaranteed up-time.
  • Familiarity with containerised deployments such as Kubernetes, and with infrastructure-as-code.
  • Comfortable with service desk platforms, reporting and automation.

Leadership & Interpersonal Skills

  • Calm and clear with customers and senior colleagues, especially when things go wrong.
  • Uses data to manage performance and to make the case for change.
  • Builds trust across Engineering, Delivery and Client Success, and gets things done without relying on authority.
  • Thinks beyond their own function, and is comfortable representing operations at leadership and Group level.
  • Fluent Business English communication.

Desirable

  • Hands-on experience with Zoho Desk or a comparable service desk platform.
  • Experience introducing AI-assisted support, knowledge-centred support or self-service.
  • ITIL 4 certification.
  • Additional languages, particularly French, German, Italian.
  • Experience supporting customers in regulated sectors such as financial services and insurance, and familiarity with ISO 27001 and SOC 2.

jobs.title: 🇩🇪 Product Engineer / Entwickler (100% Remote) – Deutsch fließend
jobs.description:
In den meisten Firmen bekommt ein Entwickler ein Ticket, baut es und nimmt sich das nächste. Mit dem Kunden hat jemand anderes geredet, was gebaut wird, hat jemand anderes entschieden, und ob es am Ende geholfen hat, fragt keiner.

Wir suchen Entwickler, die die ganze Arbeit machen wollen: mit den Leuten reden, die die Software nutzen, entscheiden, was gebaut wird, es bauen und dranbleiben, bis es für sie funktioniert. Das meinen wir mit Product Engineer. Den Begriff haben wir von PostHog, die ihn in ihrem Product Engineer Handbook gut beschreiben.

Unsere Kunden sind Hausverwaltungen in Deutschland. Du sprichst direkt mit ihnen, deshalb ist fließendes Deutsch für diese Stelle Pflicht.

Über uns

ist Software für Hausverwaltungen in Deutschland. Inbox, CRM, Dokumente, Telefonie, Videocalls, Team-Chat und KI-Agenten in einer Plattform, damit Hausverwalter ihre tägliche Arbeit an einem Ort erledigen. Wir sind ein kleines Team mit Sitz in Worms und arbeiten komplett remote. Wir finanzieren uns selbst und sind profitabel.

Was ein Product Engineer bei uns macht

  • Du redest mit Kunden. Du liest die Supportanfragen und das Feedback zu deinem Bereich, schaust dir an, wie Kunden ihn nutzen, und sprichst direkt mit ihnen, auf Deutsch. Niemand filtert das für dich.

  • Du entscheidest, was gebaut wird. Für deinen Bereich legst du fest, was als Nächstes kommt, nach dem, was Kunden brauchen und was für die Firma wichtig ist. Du schreibst auf, warum, damit das Team folgen und Feedback geben kann.

  • Du lieferst früh. Die erste Version geht an ein paar Kunden, sobald sie nützlich ist. Dann verbesserst du sie nach dem, was sie sagen und tun.

  • Du baust alles. Datenmodell, Backend, Frontend und UI. Das Ergebnis muss aufgeräumt, einfach und verständlich sein, nicht nur funktionieren.

  • Du machst den Support für deinen Bereich. Wenn etwas kaputt ist oder ein Kunde nicht weiterkommt, behebst du es und sagst ihm Bescheid.

  • Du prüfst, ob es funktioniert hat. Deine Arbeit ist nicht fertig, wenn das Feature live ist. Du schaust, ob Kunden es nutzen und ob es ihr Problem gelöst hat.

  • Du automatisierst, was geht. Wenn ein Kunde eine Supportfrage stellt, trägst du die Antwort in unsere Wissensdatenbank ein und passt unseren internen Agenten an, damit es beim nächsten Mal von selbst läuft. Vieles läuft bei uns schon automatisch, Bugfixes werden bereits halbautomatisch bearbeitet, und wir automatisieren weiter.

Beispiele, woran du arbeiten könntest

  • Ein Kunde will seine alte Dateiablage in unsere Dokumentenverwaltung holen, mit eigener Ordnerstruktur und tausenden Dokumenten, schnell und mit KI-Unterstützung. Du schaust dir an, wie er seine Dateien sortiert hat, baust den Import als allgemeines Feature für alle Kunden, richtest ihn für ihn ein und testest ihn mit seiner Ordnerstruktur. Danach prüfst du, ob die KI jedes Dokument dem richtigen Gebäude, der richtigen Wohnung oder dem richtigen Kontakt zugeordnet hat, und korrigierst, was nicht passt.

  • Ein Kunde meldet, dass der Inbox-Agent einem Mieter eine falsche Antwort gegeben hat. Du schaust dir an, was der Agent gemacht hat, korrigierst das Tool oder seine Anweisungen und gibst dem Kunden Bescheid.

  • Nur wenige Kunden bauen eigene Agenten in der Sandbox. Du findest heraus, warum, über die Daten und Gespräche mit Kunden, machst die Einrichtung einfacher und prüfst, ob danach mehr Kunden sie nutzen.

  • Hausverwalter machen dieselbe Aufgabe fünfzigmal am Tag und brauchen dafür zu viele Klicks. Du merkst das, redest mit ihnen darüber, wie sie arbeiten, und machst es schneller.

Unser Tech-Stack

Alles ist TypeScript, vom Datenbankschema bis zum Frontend.

Backend: Convex (Datenbank & Serverless Functions)

Frontend: Next.js, React, Tailwind, shadcn/ui

Agenten: Vercel AI SDK, LiveKit für Telefonie

Du baust mit Claude und bekommst so viele KI-Tokens, wie du brauchst.

Gehalt

  • 1.500 – 3.000 $ pro Monat brutto, mit Luft nach oben in den nächsten Monaten und Jahren

  • Unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag in deinem Wohnland über unseren Partner Deel (EOR)

Benefits

  • 100 % remote

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten

  • Selbst finanziert und profitabel, kein Investorengeld, das verbrannt werden muss

  • Kleines Team, was du baust, geht live

  • Schnelle Entscheidungen, keine unnötigen Meetings und keine Freigabeschleifen

Unser Gesundheitsprogramm

  • Einzelzimmer im Krankenhaus, weltweiter Schutz

  • Freie Arzt- und Facharztwahl, keine Gesundheitsprüfung, Vorerkrankungen spielen keine Rolle

  • Partner und Kinder sind mitversichert

  • Operationen, Krebsbehandlung, MRT/CT/PET und Diagnostik voll abgedeckt

  • Zahnbehandlung und Zahn-OP zu 90 % abgedeckt

  • 675 $ pro Jahr für Physiotherapie, Osteopathie, Chiropraktik und Akupunktur

  • 100 $ Krankenhaustagegeld pro Nacht, bis zu 20 Nächte

  • Medikamente, Impfungen, Brillen/Kontaktlinsen, häusliche Pflege und Krankentransport abgedeckt

Unsere Grundprinzipien

  • Speed of Implementation: Wir setzen schnell um. Eine erste Version geht früh live und wird mit dem Feedback der Kunden besser.

  • Radikale Ehrlichkeit: Wir sagen offen, was ist, im Team und gegenüber unseren Kunden. Gerade dann, wenn es unangenehm ist.

  • Hohe Ansprüche an die eigene Arbeit und an die der anderen

Requirements

Voraussetzungen

  • Fließendes Deutsch (mindestens C1), du kannst mit Kunden telefonieren und schreiben

  • Gutes Englisch

  • Mehr als ein Jahr Erfahrung mit Code, der produktiv im Einsatz ist

Worauf wir achten

  • Dir ist wichtiger, dass Kunden ihre Arbeit erledigt bekommen, als die perfekte Umsetzung.

  • Du hast ein gutes Auge für Gestaltung und UI. Du lieferst nicht einfach, was die KI erzeugt, sondern arbeitest an der Oberfläche, bis sie aufgeräumt und für die Nutzer so einfach und verständlich wie möglich ist.

  • Du machst Dinge fertig. Ein Feature, das zu 80 % fertig ist, hilft niemandem, deshalb bleibst du dran, bis es gut funktioniert.

  • Du hast eine Meinung dazu, was gebaut werden soll, und begründest sie mit dem, was Kunden sagen und tun. Wenn das Feedback etwas anderes sagt, änderst du deine Meinung.

  • Du nimmst Feedback gut an und gibst selbst ehrliches Feedback.

  • Du schreibst klar. Als Remote-Team arbeiten wir viel schriftlich: Issues, kurze Vorschläge, PR-Beschreibungen.

  • Du verstehst die Grundlagen des Geschäfts: wer unsere Kunden sind, wofür sie zahlen und warum sie bleiben.

  • Du schreibst fast deinen gesamten Code mit KI und verstehst Architektur gut genug, um zu beurteilen, was sie schreibt.

  • Du automatisierst eine Aufgabe lieber, als sie zweimal zu machen.

  • Du bist Generalist und lernst schnell Neues.

Schön zu haben

  • Du hast ein eigenes Produkt oder Nebenprojekt gebaut, das echte Menschen genutzt haben, oder schon direkt mit Kunden gearbeitet.

  • Erfahrung mit Datenbankdesign und der Optimierung von Abfragen nach Geschwindigkeit und Kosten

  • Erfahrung mit Agenten, Queues und lang laufenden Workflows im Produktivbetrieb

Die Stelle passt nicht zu dir, wenn

  • du willst, dass jemand anderes entscheidet, was du baust, und dir Tickets gibt

  • du lieber nichts mit Kunden oder Support zu tun haben willst

  • du Code wochenlang polieren willst, bevor ihn jemand sieht

  • du gern zur nächsten Idee springst, bevor die letzte wirklich funktioniert

So stellen wir ein

  1. Kennenlerngespräch

  2. Interview mit unserem Gründer über deinen Werdegang und das, was du gebaut hast

  3. Referenzgespräch mit einer früheren Führungskraft

  4. Angebot

Mehr über das, was wir bauen, siehst du auf unserem YouTube-Kanal.

Are you a person of compassion? An advocate for justice? Someone who stands up for the rights of the vulnerable and speaks out for the marginalized, the exploited and the forgotten? Do you believe in our calling as Christians to welcome the least of these and love our neighbor?
If you answered ‘yes’, to any of the above, World Relief, and millions of people around the world need you.
At this pivotal moment in time, we are rapidly expanding and growing our team to meet the increasing needs of our world. We are looking for people who want to use their gifts and talents to make a real and tangible difference in our world and the lives of the suffering.
If you’re looking for a purpose-driven career in which you can grow your talents, while also standing up for the rights of the vulnerable, we want you to join us today.

ORGANIZATION SUMMARY

World Relief is a global Christian humanitarian organization whose mission is to boldly engage the world’s greatest crises in partnership with the church. The organization was founded in the aftermath of World War II to respond to the urgent humanitarian needs of war-torn Europe. Since then, for 80 years, across 100 countries, World Relief has partnered with local churches and communities to build a world where families thrive and communities flourish.
Today, organizational programming focuses on humanitarian and disaster response, community strengthening and resilience, and refugee & immigrant services and advocacy.

POSITION SUMMARY:

World Relief seeks a detail-oriented and mission-driven Procurement Advisor to support International Programs in ensuring that the procurement of goods, services, and works across Country Offices is compliant, transparent, well-documented, and aligned with donor requirements and organizational policy. This role serves as a key resource for Country Offices navigating procurement planning, supplier vetting, sourcing, and purchase execution, while safeguarding the segregation of duties and internal controls that protect World Relief and its donors. Current offices are located in Burundi, Chad, DRC, Haiti, Rwanda, South Sudan, Sudan and Ukraine.

  • Serve as a point of contact for Country Offices and Home Office staff on procurement questions, ensuring procurement actions comply with the Procurement Policy, Procurement and Logistics Manual, donor regulations, and local law.

  • Support review of procurement exceptions, including emergency procurements, sole source justifications, and grant-funded purchase requirements.
  • Contribute to the ongoing development and maintenance of procurement tools, templates, training materials, the internal procurement module and procurement components of grant proposals.
  • Lead the organization-wide rollout of the updated Procurement Policy and Procurement and Logistics Manual.
  • Design and deliver training on the new procurement guidance and corresponding procurement module.
  • Build a training curriculum and onboarding package for procurement so that new staff and newly appointed procurement focal points are consistently trained on policy, thresholds, procurement methods, and documentation requirements.

  • Committed to the mission, vision, and values of World Relief
  • Desire to serve and empower the Church to impact vulnerable communities
  • Able to affirm and/or acknowledge World Reliefs Core Beliefs, Statement of Faith, Christian Identity and National Association of Evangelicals' For the Health of The Nation document

  • Working knowledge of procurement principles such as value for money, competition, fairness, and segregation of duties, and familiarity with donor procurement requirements (e.g., Uniform Guidance / 2 CFR 200) is strongly preferred
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills, with the ability to maintain accurate records and documentation across multiple offices and projects
  • Demonstrated experience designing and delivering training and leading the rollout of new policies or processes across multiple offices or countries, including remote and cross-cultural audiences
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate procurement guidance clearly to non-procurement staff and to build collaborative relationships with Country Office and Home Office colleagues
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, SharePoint) and comfort learning procurement or supplier database systems

  • Experience working across multiple countries or cultures in a Home Office support role

Paid social is how we grow, and our creative team works in pods: a strategist owns an angle, writes the concepts, scripts and briefs, and works with dedicated AI-first editors who bring them to life. We are adding strategists to two pods, each owning one angle, so that every angle has one person who knows it better than anyone else.

What you will own

  • One angle inside a pod. Research, concepts, scripts and briefs for it, and the iteration loop with your editors.

  • Weekly output. Around five net-new concepts and ten iterations a week, briefed clearly enough that editors can execute without going back and forth.

  • The numbers for your angle. Hit rate and new-customer ROAS, read in Triple Whale, with a weekly summary of what you tested and what you learned.

  • Your editors' time. You decide what they make and in what order, and you give them feedback that makes the next version better.

What this role is not

This is not a media buying role, not a content or organic role, and not a video editing role. You write and direct; your editors produce. It is also not an agency seat: one brand, one angle, all the way down.

Your pod lead.

    • Encourage trans communities to apply.
    • Review, score, and provide feedback on applications.
    • Make collective funding decisions.
    • Recommend grantmaking priorities and advise on strategy as relevant.
  • Strictly uphold ITF confidentiality and conflict-of-interest policies.

4. Profile of the Activists we are Seeking
Before deciding to apply, please confirm that:

  • You are committed to advancing trans rights and building sustainable trans movements.
  • Your peers consider you credible and trustworthy.
  • You value participatory grantmaking and collective, movement-accountable decision-making.

5. What “trans” means at ITF

We use “trans” as a political term for people whose gender identity or expression differs from their sex assigned at birth, including binary and non-binary identities and culturally specific identities worldwide. We do not privilege any identity or terminology over another.

6. Time Commitment

  • Annual training: 3–5 hours.
  • Application review: 30–50 applications over ~6 weeks (~50 hours/year).
  • Annual meeting: 6 days + travel (in-person or virtual).

7. Candidate Qualifications

Essential

  • Identify as trans (refer to item 5 above).
  • Minimum 3 years of direct trans activism, ideally as a regional and/or international level.
  • Recognized by trans activists in your region as a community activist/leader.
  • Fluency (spoken and written) in English or Spanish.
  • Able and willing to work in a diverse environment (activists and donors).
  • Passport enabling international travel (for in-person meetings).
  • Reliable in meeting tasks and deadlines.
  • Experience managing and reporting on grants for trans work.

8. Conflict of Interest

GMP members (and immediate family members) may not be significantly involved in any group applying to ITF during their tenure and may not benefit financially from assessed or existing ITF grants (See ITF Conflict of Interest Policy). Please note that this means that if you are part of/involved in an organization and selected as a member of the GMP, the organization will not be eligible to apply for grants during their tenure.

9. Term & Compensation

  • Term: Three (3) years, appointed by the Board.
  • Compensation:USD $1,500 per one-year grant cycle, plus covered travel and per diem for ITF meetings.

10. Selection Process

The Board will appoint seven activists with attention to diversity across gender identities/expressions and inclusion of further-marginalized groups within trans communities. We highly encourage trans men and trans masculine folks to apply.

11. How to Apply

Please submit an application in BambooHR by November 30, 2026.

We intend to inform all candidates of our decisions by January 2027.

1. Convocatoria para nuevas personas integrantes del PCA

El Fondo Internacional Trans (FIT) busca activistas comprometides para formar parte de su Panel de Concesión de Apoyos (PCA) . Las personas solicitantes pueden residir y organizarse en cualquier región del mundo.

2. Acerca del FIT

El Fondo Internacional Trans (FIT) es un fondo participativo de apoyos financieros liderado por activistas trans y donantes que lo apoyan. Proporcionamos recursos a grupos liderados por personas trans en todo el mundo para promover los derechos humanos, la autodeterminación, el bienestar y el empoderamiento de los movimientos, especialmente para aquellos grupos con acceso limitado a financiación.

3. Función del PCA

El PCA revisa las solicitudes que cumplen los requisitos y toma decisiones de financiamiento acordes con la misión, los valores y las prioridades de FIT. Las decisiones del PCA son definitivas, a la espera de la ratificación de la junta directiva.

Las principales responsabilidades del panel de concesión de apoyos son:

  • Participar en la capacitación en línea del PCA.
  • Participar en una reunión anual presencial de 6 días (la ubicación varía) o en su equivalente virtual.
  • Participar en los debates en línea y en al menos el 75% de las reuniones en línea programadas.
  • Liderar las tareas de concesión de apoyos financieros:
    • Alentar a las comunidades trans a presentar una solicitud.
    • Revisar, calificar y proporcionar comentarios sobre las solicitudes.
    • Tomar decisiones colectivas sobre el financiamiento.
    • Recomendar prioridades en la concesión de apoyos financieros y asesorar sobre la estrategia pertinente.
  • Respetar estrictamente las políticas de confidencialidad y de conflicto de intereses del FIT.

4. Perfil de las personas activistas que buscamos
Antes de decidirse a presentar su solicitud, confirme que:

  • Tienes compromiso con el avance de los derechos de las personas trans y la construcción de movimientos trans sostenibles.
  • Tus pares te consideran una persona creíble y digna de confianza.
  • Valoras la concesión participativa de apoyos financieros y la toma de decisiones colectiva y responsable ante el movimiento.

5. ¿Qué significa “trans” para el FIT?

Usamos “trans” como término político para referirnos a las personas cuya identidad o expresión de género difiere del sexo que se les asignó al nacer, incluyendo identidades binarias y no binarias, así como identidades culturalmente específicas en todo el mundo. No privilegiamos ninguna identidad ni terminología sobre otra.

6. Compromiso de tiempo

  • Capacitación anual: 3-5 horas.
  • Revisión de solicitudes: entre 30 y 50 solicitudes durante aproximadamente 6 semanas ( aproximadamente 50 horas al año ).
  • Reunión anual: 6 días + viaje (presencial o virtual).

7. Requisitos de la persona postulante

Básico

  • Identificarse como persona trans (consultar el punto 5 anterior).
  • Mínimo 3 años de activismo trans directo, idealmente a nivel regional y/o internacional.
  • Tener reconocimiento de activistas trans de tu región como activista/líder comunitarie.
  • Fluidez (oral y escrita) en inglés o español .
  • Capaz y con disposición a trabajar en un entorno diverso (activistas y donantes).
  • Pasaporte que permite viajar internacionalmente (para reuniones presenciales).
  • Confiable en el cumplimiento de tareas y plazos.
  • Experiencia en la gestión y presentación de informes sobre financiamientos para proyectos relacionados con personas trans.

8. Conflicto de intereses:

Las personas integrantes del PCA (y sus familiares directos) no podrán participar activamente en ningún grupo que solicite financiamiento al FIT durante su mandato, ni beneficiarse económicamente de los apoyos financieros del FIT ya concedidos o en curso ( véase la Política de Conflicto de Intereses de la FIT ). Ten en cuenta que, si formas parte de una organización o participas en ella y se te selecciona como integrante del PCA, dicha organización no podrá solicitar apoyos financieros durante su mandato.

9. Duración y remuneración

  • Duración del mandato: Tres (3) años, designado por la Junta.
  • Compensación:
    1.500 dólares estadounidenses por ciclo anual de apoyos financieros, además de los gastos de viaje y dietas cubiertos para las reuniones del FIT.

10. Proceso de selección:

La junta designará a siete activistas, prestando especial atención a la diversidad de identidades y expresiones de género, así como a la inclusión de grupos más marginados dentro de las comunidades trans. Alentamos encarecidamente a hombres trans y personas trans masculinas a presentar su solicitud.

11. Cómo solicitar

Por favor, envía tu solicitud a través de BambooHR antes del 30 de noviembre de 2026.

Tenemos previsto informar a todas las personas postulantes de nuestras decisiones antes de enero de 2027.

jobs.title: Hands-on Engineering Manager DevOps (GCP/Kubernetes)
jobs.description:
Location: 100% remote (EMEA)

Classification: Full-time

Pay Range: 82.000€ to 140.000€ - determined by several factors, including location

Miaplaza is dedicated to making education engaging and accessible through innovative online learning platforms. We develop personalized learning experiences for students, helping them grow in a supportive and interactive environment. Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive education curriculum platform where all students can be successful!

As an engineering manager at Miaplaza, your team will build technology with a direct impact on the lives of hundreds of thousands of students. Every step of the way, you will have the opportunity to influence our direction. Through our platforms, we create engaging, safe, and thoughtfully designed learning experiences that help children grow academically, creatively, and personally. Every feature we ship, every system we scale, and every improvement we make contributes to shaping how the next generation learns and discovers their potential. If our platform is down, a child might not go to school that day. We’re looking for leaders who want their work to matter in classrooms and homes, who care about access to quality education, and who are excited to craft technology that makes a difference in young people’s lives. Here, your impact doesn’t just power a product; it shapes future generations!

What you’ll work on:

We’re moving everything towards GCP and Kubernetes. We’re growing towards a scale that no longer matches our legacy architecture and actively investing in modernization. We’re migrating on-premise workloads to GKE, strengthening security and business continuity best practices, and moving toward platform self-service for our development teams. A core goal is to consolidate and shrink the stack, and every migration decision is measured against whether it lowers the daily burden on the team. You’ll need to work with your team balancing both platform initiatives and the operational needs of the engineering teams you serve. You’ll report to our head of engineering and be expected to split your time roughly 50/50 between people management and hands-on development. Prioritization always goes to leading and supporting your engineers. Your team will consist of four engineers.

What’s unique about management at Miaplaza:

Miaplaza is a US-based education company, which means we probably are doing things differently than you’ve done in your past experience. Here are a few differences you may notice:

  1. You will first onboard within your team as a senior engineer for 2 months. You will start to onboard as a manager during month two and will take over the team roughly at 10 weeks. This is non-negotiable as both periods of time are equally important.

  2. We expect our EMs to spend approximately 50% of their time hands-on, even after they’ve completed onboarding as a senior engineer.

  3. We emphasize the importance of pedagogical principles. A responsibility is to grow your engineers and those around you.

  4. One of such pedagogical principles is that we expect you to have full oversight into your direct reports' work; you can’t properly teach if you don’t see the process behind the output.

  5. Feedback is the norm. You’ll be expected to give meaningful, specific reinforcement and constructive feedback whenever you notice something. You should also expect to receive feedback. Ultimately, everything we do is optimizing ourselves, our teams, our processes, and our company to best support our students.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

  • 2+ years of experience being a mentor/leader, of which:

    • 1+ years leading a team, formally or as a tech lead

  • 7+ years of experience in DevOps, SRE, or Infrastructure Engineering, of which:

  • 3+ years running production workloads on Kubernetes (GKE preferred)

  • 3+ years of experience with a major cloud provider and Infrastructure as Code. GCP is our primary cloud and we expect senior-level knowledge of IAM, networking, KMS, GKE, CloudSQL and Secret Manager

  • 3+ years of experience operating at a Senior, Staff, or Principal Engineer level.

  • Experience with CI/CD pipeline design and operations

  • Experience with GitOps (FluxCD or ArgoCD)

  • Experience working directly with engineering teams and other managers as your customers on scoping and prioritization

  • Experience leading incident response, including running postmortems

What makes you stand out:

Experience leading a team through a significant architectural migration

Experience with consumer platforms at scale

Experience building in regulated environments

Experience operating self-hosted observability stacks (Prometheus, Thanos, Loki, Grafana, Tempo, OpenTelemetry)

Experience building internal developer platforms or self-service tooling

Experience supporting .NET/C# application deployments

Experience with database operations (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, RabbitMQ)

Experience with Istio or other service meshes

Responsibilities

  • Work with your team to design, build, and operate the infrastructure the rest of engineering depends on: clusters, pipelines, databases, edge, and observability

  • Your customers are the other engineering teams. Work with the other Engineering Managers and product development leadership to scope and prioritize platform work

  • Set the quality bar for your team. Lead by example.

  • Manage, lead, and mentor your team while working side by side with them in code quality, clean infrastructure-as-code, soft skills, best practices, etc

  • Lead team trainings, set SMART goals, hold performance reviews, and provide individual feedback recurrently to each of your devs

Our hiring process

As a remote company, we receive a large number of applicants, and finding the best fit for this role is our top priority — that’s why our process is longer than usual. At every stage, we try to be respectful of your time and grateful you’re spending it with us.

  • Application and CV Review - Our team will review your application responses and CV, then follow up with an update.

  • Initial Technical Screen (20 minutes) - A quick screening call to answer some administrative questions and confirm your basic technical knowledge. You'll be asked some administrative questions and 7 short technical questions related to the role.

  • Behavioral Interview (1 hour) - Meet with a member of our HR team to discuss your experience and share your approach throughout your career so far.

  • 1st Technical Interview (1 hour) - Meet with a member of the Infrastructure team to answer focused technical questions tailored to our work.

  • Scenario-based Technical Interview (1 hour) - Meet with a member of the Infrastructure team and the team's engineering manager to work through two hypothetical DevOps scenarios and how you would tackle them.

  • Leadership Interview (1 hour) - With our head of engineering and executive leadership.

  • Reference check - We'll reach out to the 3 references you provided, at least one being a former or current manager and any former or current direct reports.

  • Offer & background check - Once you sign your offer, we'll run a background check in accordance with applicable law.

We give honest, timely feedback at every step. Job searches are hard; we don't want to make yours harder.

Compensation and setup

The pay range for this role is €82,000 - 140,000. Miaplaza’s compensation philosophy ensures equity and competitiveness while considering regional differences in labor costs. Placement within a range is determined based on factors such as demonstrated skills, internal equity, and local labor market rates for the candidate’s geographic area.

Miaplaza is a growing, self-funded EdTech company. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. If you need accommodations at any point in the process, just let us know.

jobs.title: 🇩🇪 Softwareentwickler für Datenmigration und Kunden-Onboarding (100% Remote) – D
jobs.description:
Jede Hausverwaltung, die zu uns wechselt, kommt aus einer anderen Softwarelandschaft: ein altes Verwaltungsprogramm, ein eigenes Buchhaltungssystem, Tausende Dokumente in Ordnern auf dem Server, eine Telefonanlage und ein paar Excel-Listen, die nur eine Kollegin versteht. Kein Umzug ist wie der andere.

Dein Job ist, die ganze Firma zu uns umzuziehen. Dafür arbeitest du mit internen Tools, die wir genau für solche Umzüge gebaut haben, und baust dir mit Claude Code eigene, wenn ein Kunde etwas mitbringt, das wir noch nicht kennen. Manchmal reicht ein einmaliger Import nicht. Dann sorgst du dafür, dass die Daten in der Übergangszeit zwischen dem alten System und uns hin und her synchronisiert werden.

Dabei betreust du den Kunden persönlich, vom ersten Gespräch, bis er bei uns richtig angekommen ist. Unsere Kunden sind Hausverwaltungen in Deutschland, deshalb ist fließendes Deutsch für diese Stelle Pflicht.

Über uns

ist Software für Hausverwaltungen in Deutschland. Inbox, CRM, Dokumente, Telefonie, Videocalls, Team-Chat und KI-Agenten in einer Plattform, damit Hausverwalter ihre tägliche Arbeit an einem Ort erledigen. Wir sind ein kleines Team mit Sitz in Worms und arbeiten komplett remote. Wir finanzieren uns selbst und sind profitabel.

Was du bei uns machst

  • Du ziehst ganze Firmen um. Dokumente, Stammdaten, Buchhaltung, E-Mails, alte Vorgänge, Telefonanlage: Du holst alles aus den bisherigen Systemen zu uns, egal woher der Kunde kommt.

  • Du arbeitest mit unseren Umzugs-Tools und baust dir eigene. Für viele Systeme haben wir schon interne Tools. Bringt ein Kunde etwas mit, das wir noch nicht kennen, baust du dir mit Claude Code das passende Werkzeug, so dass der nächste Umzug damit schneller geht.

  • Du hältst altes und neues System synchron. Kann ein Kunde nicht von heute auf morgen umsteigen, laufen die Daten in der Übergangszeit zwischen seinem bisherigen System und uns hin und her, ohne dass etwas verloren geht oder doppelt ankommt.

  • Du betreust den Kunden persönlich. Vom ersten Gespräch bis zum Start bist du sein Ansprechpartner, per Videocall, Telefon und Chat. Du verstehst, wie sein Team arbeitet, und richtest die Software so ein, dass sie dazu passt.

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass alles stimmt. Am Ende liegt jedes Dokument, jeder Kontakt und jede Buchung am richtigen Platz. Das gehst du mit dem Kunden durch, bevor er umschaltet.

  • Du bleibst dran, bis der Kunde zufrieden ist. Nach dem Start schaust du, ob das Team gut mit der Software arbeitet, und klärst Probleme, bevor sie groß werden.

Beispiele, woran du arbeiten könntest

  • Eine Hausverwaltung arbeitet seit vielen Jahren mit demselben Verwaltungsprogramm. Du holst Gebäude, Einheiten, Eigentümer, Mieter und die Buchhaltung rüber, gleichst alles mit den Dokumenten ab und gehst es mit dem Kunden in einem Call durch.

Alles ist TypeScript, vom Datenbankschema bis zum Frontend.

About us

Infomineo is a pioneering global AI-enhanced research company that transforms how businesses access, analyze, and act on critical intelligence. We’ve evolved from traditional business research outsourcing to become the strategic partner that combines cutting-edge artificial intelligence with deep human expertise. We offer 3 services to our global clients (leading consulting companies, Fortune 500 companies, and government entities): AI and Data Advisory, Next-Gen Insights and Resource Scaling.   2. Our proprietary AI orchestrator.
  3. Extensive knowledge assets combining 500,000+ delivered case studies and database subscriptions.

Ready to kick start your career with us?

About this role

This role will give you the opportunity to work on high added value data governance and data quality projects, building robust data management frameworks for our clients within a growing service company.

As our Data Governance Specialist, you will help clients take control of their data assets — defining policies, enforcing quality standards, managing metadata, and deploying governance tooling. You will collaborate closely with data engineers, analysts, and client stakeholders to embed governance practices across the full data lifecycle.

What will you do?

Design, implement, and operationalize data governance frameworks across client engagements, covering the following areas:

DATA GOVERNANCE & POLICY

  • Define and implement data governance frameworks, policies, and standards tailored to client environments.
  • Establish data ownership, stewardship models, and accountability structures across business and technical teams.
  • Develop and maintain data dictionaries, business glossaries, and classification taxonomies.
  • Ensure compliance with data regulations and internal data management policies (GDPR, BCBS 239, etc.).

DATA QUALITY & LINEAGE

  • Design and implement data quality rules, profiling routines, and monitoring dashboards.
  • Investigate and remediate data quality issues across structured and unstructured data sources.
  • Map and document end-to-end data lineage to support auditability and impact analysis.
  • Define and track data quality KPIs and SLAs in collaboration with data owners.

METADATA & CATALOGUING

  • Deploy and administer data catalog and metadata management tools (e.g. Informatica, Collibra, Alation, Microsoft Purview).
  • Enrich metadata assets with business context, ownership, sensitivity classification, and usage information.
  • Drive adoption of the data catalog across business and technical teams.

TOOLING & INTEGRATION

  • Configure and operate data governance platforms, primarily Informatica (IDMC, Axon, EDC, DQ) and equivalent tools.
  • Integrate governance tooling with existing data pipelines, warehouses, and BI environments.
  • Automate data quality checks and governance workflows within ETL/ELT pipelines.

OTHER

  • Provide internal training and knowledge-sharing sessions on data governance best practices.
  • Support the Team Lead/Manager on client relationships, business development, and internal projects.

Who are you?

EDUCATION & PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

  • Master’s degree in a relevant field such as Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Management, Statistics, or Applied Mathematics.
  • Full proficiency in English + 1 additional language (French, Arabic, Spanish, German...).
  • 3 to 6 years of experience in data governance, data management, or data engineering with a strong governance focus.
  • Experience working in a consulting, financial services, or multi-client environment is a plus.

TECHNICAL SKILLS

DATA GOVERNANCE TOOLS

  • Proven hands-on experience with Informatica (IDMC / Intelligent Data Management Cloud, Axon Data Governance, Enterprise Data Catalog, Data Quality).
  • Experience with other governance and cataloguing platforms such as Collibra, Alation, Ataccama, or Microsoft Purview.
  • Familiarity with data quality tools: Great Expectations, Monte Carlo, Soda, or equivalent.

DATA ENGINEERING & QUERYING

  • Solid experience with SQL for data profiling, querying, and quality rule implementation across relational databases and data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Synapse, Redshift).
  • Experience in Python for automating data quality checks, metadata extraction, and governance workflows.
  • Understanding of ETL/ELT pipelines and ability to embed governance controls within them (dbt, Airflow, Informatica PowerCenter/IDMC).

DATA ARCHITECTURE & PLATFORMS

  • Good understanding of data platform architectures: data lake, lakehouse, and data warehouse environments.
  • Familiarity with cloud platforms and their native governance services: Azure Purview, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Google Dataplex.
  • Understanding of data modelling concepts and their impact on governance (dimensional modelling, data vault, etc.).

STANDARDS & COMPLIANCE

  • Knowledge of data governance frameworks and standards: DAMA-DMBOK, BCBS 239, GDPR, ISO 8000.
  • Experience defining and applying data classification schemes (sensitivity labels, PII tagging, retention policies).
  • Exposure to master data management (MDM) concepts and tools is a plus.

INTERPERSONAL SKILLS

  • Ability to engage and influence both technical teams and business stakeholders on data governance topics.
  • Strong analytical mindset with the ability to diagnose data quality issues and translate them into actionable remediation plans.
  • Good communication skills with the ability to document governance frameworks clearly and present findings to senior audiences.
  • Detail-oriented, rigorous, and comfortable working across multiple client contexts simultaneously.

What we offer

  • A competitive salary.
  • A great working environment.
  • A steep learning curve with interesting and diverse topics to work on.
  • A healthy work-life balance.
  • Health insurance benefits.

As Academics Leader for international markets, you will shape and lead GE HealthCare’s academic strategy outside the United States, Canada and China. Academic medical centers and research institutions adopt advanced technology early, publish, shape guidelines and train the next generation of
clinicians. When we win with academics, we influence the whole market.

You will build and personally own the commercial account strategy and executive relationships for approximately 20 strategic academic accounts, develop the International Academics commercial framework and orchestrate execution with country and zone teams. You will partner closely with Scientific Affairs under clearly defined Research-Commercial rules of engagement.

This role owns the commercial strategy, customer experience, pipeline and business results for the International Academics segment.

Focus markets include the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Spain, Japan, South Korea, Australia and India, as well as the international accounts among GE HealthCare’s top 50 global academic accounts.

At GE HealthCare, our machines, our software, our solutions, our services, and our people make a genuine difference to medical professionals and patients all over the world. That’s because we never lose sight of what healthcare really needs—the human touch.

Job Description

Your role:


Commercial academic relationships and account strategy


  • Build and maintain trusted, senior relationships with leading academic medical centers, research institutions, universities and scientific societies in the focus markets.
  • Personally own a portfolio of about 20 strategic academic collaborations, from identification and structuring through governance, delivery and renewal.
  • Develop flagship, multi-year and cross-modality commercial partnerships and enterprise solutions, including differentiated customer experience and co-location models where appropriate.
  • Use proven models from the United States and Canada and scale them to international accounts.
  • Establish reference and showcase sites that demonstrate GE HealthCare solutions, customer outcomes and innovation adoption, with any research claims or scientific outputs led and approved through Scientific Affairs and the appropriate functions.

International Academics commercial framework


  • Develop and own the international academic commercial framework: one engagement model, standard work for academic account management, rules of engagement, key performance indicators (KPIs) and governance, including executive and C-suite governance for strategic accounts.
  • Segment academic accounts, including research-active private accounts, and define targeted value propositions and growth plans for each segment.
  • Lead with differentiated entry points, such as care pathways, theranostics, photon-counting CT, nuclear medicine, AI and areas such as human performance and longevity.
  • Continuously improve the framework based on results, customer feedback and learnings from the United States and Canada.

Country orchestration


  • Work hand in hand with country and zone leadership teams to embed academics in every focus country plan and in plans for the top 50 global academic accounts.
  • Orchestrate the framework across countries, aligning country commercial teams, segment and care pathway leaders, product teams and services behind shared academic priorities.
  • Coordinate a virtual network of country academic account leads, clinical specialists and regional academic leaders, with clear roles and accountability.
  • Share best practices and results across markets, and escalate and resolve barriers to collaboration quickly. Scientific Affairs partnership
  • Partner closely with Scientific Affairs while maintaining clear separation of commercial and research activities and following the agreed Research-Commercial rules of engagement.
  • Align commercial stakeholder mapping and engagement plans with the Scientific Affairs-led KOL framework.
  • Support adoption of new product introductions at academic accounts through coordinated commercial launch planning, customer readiness and white-glove application and service support
  • Translate existing, approved evidence and scientific outputs into compliant commercial value propositions and customer communications in partnership with Scientific Affairs, Marketing, Legal, Regulatory and Compliance.
  • Identify customer needs or opportunities related to research, grants, evidence generation, publications, symposia or scientific meetings and refer them to Scientific Affairs for assessment, ownership and execution.

Commercial performance


  • Own orders, revenue and margin targets for the international academic segment, and grow GE HealthCare’s share of wallet in target academic accounts.
  • Build and manage the international academic commercial pipeline, and run a disciplined cadence of account plans, opportunity reviews and forecasts. • Work with country commercial teams to close large, multi-year academic deals.
  • Ensure all engagements follow research-commercial policies and quality, regulatory and integrity standards.

Your profile:


Required

  • A master’s degree or higher, such as a PhD, MD, MBA, MS or MPH, or equivalent professional experience
  • Significant progressive commercial or general-management leadership experience in complex healthcare, medtech or academic-health-system environments
  • Established, credible relationships with academic leaders, KOLs and research institutions in several of the focus markets
  • A proven record of developing and closing large, multi-year, multi-modality healthcare solutions or strategic commercial partnerships
  • Experience designing and rolling out frameworks, engagement models or standard work across multiple countries
  • Strong understanding of academic health-system operations, capital and technology investment decisions, procurement and complex enterprise selling
  • The ability to orchestrate complex, matrixed organizations across countries and functions, including close work with scientific, medical, legal and compliance teams
  • Excellent executive engagement, communication and negotiation skills
  • A strong commitment to Research-Commercial separation, compliance and integrity
  • Fluent English, and willingness to travel internationally about 50 percent of the time

Preferred

  • Experience leading academic or enterprise accounts across Europe and Asia-Pacific
  • Knowledge of advanced imaging, theranostics, nuclear medicine, photon-counting CT or AI
  • Experience using Salesforce, commercial analytics and data-visualization tools to drive account execution
  • Additional languages relevant to the focus markets

This role can be remote based anywhere in Europe or EEU.


About us

jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Role

Serve as the on-duty commander for Alpaca's most critical incidents, directing cross-functional response to restore service quickly, keeping the right people engaged and informed, and making sure every incident leaves behind something the organisation can act on.

You do not fix the outage. You make the response reliable: correct severity, the right engineers in the room, mitigation that does not stall, leaders informed in time, and follow-up work that survives the call.

Things You Get To Do

  • Command incidents end to end. Take command from declaration to mitigation, keeping responders focused on stopping customer and partner impact as fast as possible. Run the bridge, keep observers out of the responders' way, and name a stall out loud when you see one.
  • Classify and hold the line on severity. Set severity at declaration and re-check it as facts arrive. Risk advises on financial and regulatory materiality; the call is yours.
  • Engage the right people, fast. Identify the owning team by service, symptom and blast radius, page them, and expand the responder set the moment the first team is wrong or not enough. When a page goes unanswered, escalate - and escalate the escalation. Bring in the leaders who must make business calls: feature flags, traffic shedding, failover, freeze-or-ship.
  • Hold the bridge, and protect the people fixing it. Keep engineering and technical support uninterrupted - questions from stakeholders, partners and executives come to you. Be the single source of truth to the partner communications team on impact, severity and timing: you decide when a status page update or partner contact is needed, they write and send it, and chasing a late or stale update is yours.
  • Run follow-the-sun handoffs. Deliver warm, high-fidelity handoffs across regions: current impact and severity, mitigation path and next actions, who is in the room, outstanding decisions, and what must not be dropped. The incoming commander confirms ownership before you step away - command never goes dark at a region boundary.
  • Close the loop, on the clock. Maintain the timeline of facts as the incident runs rather than reconstructing it afterwards - in a regulated business that record has to hold up long after the call ends. Once mitigated, make sure a blameless retrospective is scheduled with a named owner and a timebox, and record where the cause sits - that choice sets which follow-up items are mandatory. Every action item needs a real ticket, one named accountable, a priority and a category, delivered inside the agreed service level. If a postmortem produces nothing but low-priority items, treat that as a signal the analysis stopped early and escalate to SRE rather than passing it on.
  • Automate the coordination away. Coordination is the part of this job that should eventually belong to a machine. Every manual prompt you send - the update that is due, the question nobody answered, the partner nobody contacted - is a candidate for automation, and the direction we are heading is AI handling the routine so commanders can spend their attention on judgement. You get us there by working to the decision trees, saying where they are wrong, and being honest about which of your instincts are actually rules.

Who You Are (Must-Haves)

  • 4+ years commanding or co-commanding high-severity incidents in a production engineering, SRE or technical operations environment.
  • You direct technical responders under pressure without being the person writing the fix.

  • You will work a regional coverage window as part of a global 24x7 Incident Commander roster.

jobs.title: Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Fingerprint empowers enterprises to detect and stop online fraud with the world’s most accurate device intelligence. We lead our industry with bleeding-edge identification capabilities and work on turning new ideas and discoveries in the fraud detection space into reality. Our customers range from innovative startups to leading enterprise companies, including Plaid, Dropbox, and Booking.com.

Fingerprint is a globally dispersed, 100% remote company. We were named on on the 2026 Forbes Best Startup Employers list and ranked #803 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of America’s fastest-growing private companies.

We have raised $77M and are backed by Craft Ventures (Tesla, Facebook, Airbnb ), Nexus Venture Partners ( Postman, Apollo.io,MinIO, Druva) and Uncorrelated Ventures ( Redis, Rollbar, Gradle).

Location Preference: Remote, US and EMEA preferred but not required

About The Role:

We’re looking for a Design Engineer to own how Fingerprint looks, feels, and works on the web. You’ll design and build fingerprint.com, communicating our vision of a fraud-free internet and showcasing Fingerprint’s device intelligence platform through clear, compelling experiences for developers and the teams evaluating our product.

We’ve formed a dedicated website engineering pod to raise the website to the level of the best product sites on the internet, and you’ll join it as the person who owns the overall look and feel. You’ll work alongside the pod’s design engineers and engineers, plus partners across Design, Marketing, and Growth, taking projects from early concepts through production. You’ll move between design tools like Figma and the browser, explore new visual directions, and build interactions that help people understand what Fingerprint can do.

This role leans toward design. We’re looking for exceptional taste and craft, paired with the engineering skills to implement your own designs directly in the browser with speed and attention to detail. You care about typography and layout as much as clean code and a performant, accessible experience. You’re naturally curious, you start things without waiting for a ticket, and you’re excited to use AI to explore designs rapidly. You’ll be given near-unlimited tokens to go crazy. You’ll help shape the website’s design system, propose improvements, and see your work through to launch and beyond.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the look and feel of fingerprint.com, designing and building core website experiences, including our homepage, product pages, pricing, and navigation, from initial exploration through responsive implementation and launch.
  • Turn technical product concepts into clear visual explanations and interactive demos that help developers understand and evaluate Fingerprint.
  • Refine typography, composition, motion, and interaction details to make the website feel distinctive and cohesive across devices.
  • Build and maintain reusable components, design tokens, and page patterns that connect our visual language to production code and help the team ship faster.
  • Build accessible, mobile-friendly, performant experiences that follow web best practices, working with the website pod on maintainable code, page speed, and consistent behavior across browsers.
  • Collaborate with Marketing and Growth on product launches and website experiments, turning clear objectives into design concepts and production code.
  • Carry work through review, testing, and release, then use feedback and website data to improve usability and conversion.
  • Take initiative: contribute ideas proactively, share prototypes early, and make thoughtful tradeoffs between creative ambition, implementation effort, and delivery.
  • Find creative ways to use AI to ship high-quality work at speeds not possible with human-only input, such as machine-readable design specs, skills or internal tools, and evolve those workflows as the tools change.

Qualifications:

  • 6–10 years of related working experience designing and building for the web, with a track record of owning projects end to end as a hands-on individual contributor.
  • An active portfolio website and/or GitHub/social profile showing websites or interactive experiences that demonstrate exceptional design taste and production frontend development. We want to understand what you personally designed and built.
  • Strong visual and interaction design fundamentals, including typography, hierarchy, spacing, composition, and responsive layouts.
  • Strong HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and TypeScript skills, with experience building production websites using React and modern web frameworks like Astro.
  • Hands-on experience with canvas animations and shaders, and comfort prototyping motion and interactions directly in the browser.
  • Fluency in Figma and a habit of exploring ideas both in Figma and in code, using AI coding tools to iterate.
  • A practical understanding of web performance, accessibility, and browser behavior, with the ability to diagnose and resolve issues in your own work.
  • Experience turning an open-ended brief into a finished experience, explaining design and technical decisions, and incorporating feedback from different disciplines.
  • The ability to work independently and collaborate clearly in a distributed team, with care for both the quality of the result and the pace of delivery.
  • Experience using AI-first workflows to accelerate parts of the design process and enable other teammates to ship high-quality assets.
  • Preferred experience with , WebGL, motion.dev, and Blender or 3D animation
  • Technical B2B product experience highly preferred
  • Astro, interactive data visualization is a plus
  • Role requires proficiency with macOS and comfort working fully remotely using tools such as Slack, Google Workspace, and Zoom.

At Fingerprint, we believe in pay transparency — it's part of how we operate as a distributed, remote-first team. Salaries are based on function, level, and geographic location, benchmarked against similar stage growth companies.

Because this role is open across the United States and EMEA region and can be based anywhere our team members work from, the salary range reflects that geographic breadth: $103,000 - $180,000 USD.

Some example salaries for specific locations are below:

New York City: $150,000 - $180,000 USD

Chicago: $126,000 - $145,000 USD

United Kingdom/Ireland: $103,000 - $119,000 USD

Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including the successful candidate's location, experience, and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

Due to regulatory and security reasons, there’s a small number of countries where we cannot have Fingerprint teammates based. Additionally, because Fingerprint is an all-remote company and people can join our workforce from almost any country, we do not sponsor visas. Fingerprint teammates need to be authorized to work from their home location.

We are dedicated to creating an inclusive work environment for everyone. We embrace and celebrate the unique experiences, perspectives and cultural backgrounds that each employee brings to our workplace. Fingerprint strives to foster an environment where our employees feel respected, valued and empowered, and our team members are at the forefront in helping us promote and sustain an inclusive workplace. We highly encourage people from underrepresented groups in tech to apply.

If you are applying as a resident of the EU, please read our GDPR notice here.

jobs.description:
EMCD is a leading technology company in the crypto industry, best known as the largest mining pool in Eastern Europe. We are expanding globally and building a comprehensive ecosystem of crypto services, including payment infrastructure, custody, mining solutions and enterprise-grade tools for businesses and institutions.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Go Developer to own the blockchain rails that move user funds across our ecosystem. This is a hands-on engineering role at the core of every deposit and withdrawal: connecting new networks, keeping the ledger accurate to the last unit, and resolving incidents before they turn into losses. It suits someone who enjoys untangling complex systems and treats reliability with real money as a craft.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain blockchain rail services: deposits, withdrawals, address management and node interaction.
  • Integrate new networks and coins end to end, from analysis to production, covering nodes, address derivation, precision, fees and confirmations.
  • Own the ledger layer: entries, balances, holds, and reconciliation between on-chain data and internal accounting.
  • Take full ownership of the deposit and withdrawal rails, including incidents such as uncredited deposits, stuck or duplicate withdrawals and refunds: investigate them using production and on-chain data, then fix the root causes.
  • Contribute to design sessions, write HLDs and ADRs, and break work down into clear tasks.
  • Review code, mentor teammates and take part in the team's on-call rotation.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of commercial Go development in production.
  • Hands-on experience with blockchains, covering both the UTXO model (BTC and its forks) and the account model (EVM, TRON): node RPC, confirmations, reorgs, fees and mempool.
  • Solid understanding of keys and addresses: HD derivation (BIP32/44), address formats and transaction signing.
  • Experience with ledger and double-entry accounting: entries, holds (authorize capture/void), balance invariants and reconciliation.
  • Strong grasp of reliability when handling money: idempotency, double-spend protection, the outbox pattern, at-least-once delivery with deduplication, and eventual consistency.
  • PostgreSQL expertise: transactions, locking and isolation levels.
  • Distributed systems experience with gRPC and RabbitMQ or Kafka.
  • Working knowledge of Kubernetes and the monitoring stack (Prometheus, Grafana).

  • Ability to write clear HLDs and ADRs and well-structured Jira tasks rather than one-liners.
  • Proactive communication in cross-team threads and calls, with clear ownership of your scope.
  • Working English for documentation and written communication.

What We Offer

  • Real impact and ownership in fintech and crypto projects.

jobs.title: Sales Engineer EMEA - Remote (Contract to Hire)
jobs.description:
About DigiStor

DigiStor develops secure data-at-rest solutions for enterprise, government, defense, and other security-conscious organizations. Our portfolio includes secure and self-encrypting SSDs, removable NVMe storage solutions, and technologies designed for demanding client, workstation, server, and edge environments.

Role Overview

The Field Engineer, EMEA will be DigiStor's primary customer-facing technical resource supporting two EMEA Sales Representatives.

The role combines technical pre-sales, solution design, product demonstrations, platform qualification, and field support. You will help customers select, evaluate, integrate, and deploy DigiStor secure-storage solutions within Dell Technologies and HP/HPE client, workstation, server, and edge platforms.

You will work closely with customers, channel partners, OEM contacts, Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Testing, and Technical Support. Your purpose will be to remove technical barriers, reduce risk, and help convert qualified opportunities into successful deployments.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Pre-Sales

  • Partner with two EMEA Sales Representatives throughout the customer engagement lifecycle.
  • Lead technical discovery sessions to understand the customer's platform, workload, security, performance, environmental, and compliance requirements.
  • Recommend the most appropriate DigiStor product, capacity, form factor, interface, and security configuration.
  • Translate complex storage and security concepts into clear business and operational benefits.
  • Deliver technical presentations, product demonstrations, workshops, and architecture discussions.
  • Support customer responses, proposals, RFIs, RFPs, technical questionnaires, and tender submissions.
  • Help Sales identify technical risks, dependencies, and qualification requirements early in the opportunity.

Platform and Solution Engineering

  • Advise customers on the integration of DigiStor solutions into Dell and HP/HPE servers, workstations, desktops, laptops, and edge platforms.
  • Assess compatibility across NVMe, SATA, PCIe, BIOS/UEFI, operating systems, firmware, physical form factors, power, cooling, and thermal requirements.
  • Support storage technologies and form factors including M.2, U.2, U.3, E1.S, SATA, and removable NVMe solutions.
  • Develop recommended configurations, compatibility guidance, bills of material, and solution documentation.
  • Work with DigiStor Engineering and Testing teams to coordinate platform validation and resolve compatibility questions.

Evaluations and Proofs of Concept

  • Define and manage customer evaluations, proof-of-concept activities, and product qualification plans.
  • Establish clear technical success criteria with customers and Sales.
  • Assist with product installation, configuration, testing, benchmarking, and results interpretation.
  • Capture diagnostic information, reproduce reported issues where possible, and coordinate escalation to the appropriate Engineering or Support team.
  • Maintain ownership and clear customer communication through technical resolution and handover.

Secure-Storage Expertise

  • Explain secure-storage technologies including hardware encryption, self-encrypting drives, TCG Opal, pre-boot authentication, key management, and secure erase.
  • Help customers understand relevant certification and compliance requirements, including FIPS, Common Criteria, TAA, NATO, and regional security programmes.
  • Ensure that technical claims and recommendations accurately reflect product capabilities and certification status.
  • Support customers operating in regulated, government, defence, financial-services, healthcare, and critical-infrastructure environments.

Partner and Field Enablement

  • Develop strong technical relationships with customers, distributors, resellers, integrators, and OEM stakeholders across EMEA.
  • Deliver technical training and enablement sessions for channel and sales partners.
  • Create and maintain technical guides, configuration notes, FAQs, reference architectures, and field playbooks.
  • Bring structured customer feedback, competitive intelligence, and emerging requirements back to DigiStor's Product and Engineering teams.
  • Represent DigiStor at customer meetings, partner events, industry events, and technical briefings.

Required Experience and Knowledge

  • Proven experience as a Field Engineer, Sales Engineer, Systems Engineer, Solutions Architect, Field Applications Engineer, or Technical Pre-Sales Engineer.
  • Strong working knowledge of Dell Technologies and HP/HPE client, workstation, and server platforms.
  • Practical understanding of enterprise storage, SSDs, NVMe, SATA, PCIe, firmware, BIOS/UEFI, and storage-device integration.
  • Experience supporting both Windows and Linux environments.
  • Ability to diagnose hardware, firmware, operating-system, performance, and compatibility issues.
  • Experience planning and delivering customer evaluations or proofs of concept.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with infrastructure architects, security teams, IT operations, procurement teams, partners, and senior decision-makers.
  • Strong written and spoken English.
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly across EMEA.
  • Ability to work independently within a geographically distributed organisation.

Desirable Experience

  • Knowledge of self-encrypting drives, TCG Opal, AES-256 encryption, pre-boot authentication, and data-at-rest security.
  • Familiarity with FIPS 140-2/140-3, Common Criteria, CSfC, TAA, NATO, UK, or European security requirements.
  • Experience with Dell OEM, HP/HPE, or other major hardware-manufacturer ecosystems.
  • Experience with storage-testing and diagnostic tools such as NVMe CLI, SMART utilities, fio, Iometer, and operating-system hardware tools.
  • Experience supporting government, defence, financial-services, healthcare, industrial, or other regulated customers.
  • Knowledge of removable storage, rugged systems, edge computing, or industrial computing environments.
  • Fluency in an additional European language.

Core Competencies

  • Customer focus: Builds trust and remains accountable throughout the technical engagement.
  • Technical depth: Understands systems, storage, security, and platform integration at a practical level.
  • Commercial awareness: Connects technical recommendations to customer value and sales outcomes.
  • Problem-solving: Approaches complex technical issues logically and remains effective under pressure.
  • Communication: Explains technical subjects clearly to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
  • Ownership: Drives activities through to completion and communicates progress proactively.
  • Collaboration: Works effectively across Sales, Engineering, Product, Testing, Support, and external partners.
  • Adaptability: Learns new technologies quickly and remains current with changing platforms and standards.

Measures of Success

Success in this position will be demonstrated through:

  • Effective technical coverage of EMEA sales opportunities.
  • Faster and more accurate qualification of customer requirements.
  • Successful customer evaluations and proofs of concept.
  • Reduced technical risk and fewer late-stage compatibility issues.
  • Strong customer, partner, and Sales satisfaction.
  • Clear and timely resolution or escalation of field issues.
  • Improved technical enablement and knowledge across the EMEA partner network.
  • High-quality field feedback that contributes to DigiStor's product and technology roadmap.

DigiStor is committed to building an inclusive working environment. Employment decisions are based on business needs, role requirements, and individual qualifications.

jobs.title: Quality Assurance Rater - Spanish speakers in Spain
jobs.description:
Join our elite team of Senior Raters as a critical contributor to high-quality validation data that directly influences product development and quality assurance for leading search engines and AI technologies.

This flexible, remote opportunity allows you to apply your analytical and research skills to evaluate search results and AI-generated content while contributing to the development of high-quality AI systems.

 

A Day in the Life of a Quality Assurance Rater

In this role, you'll conduct analytical assessments of search results and AI responses, providing ratings and feedback that help improve AI model performance and search quality.

Your work will maintain high quality standards and deliver the accuracy our clients depend on.

You'll evaluate a variety of rating tasks, analyze content with attention to detail, conduct research to support rating decisions, and identify guideline gaps or task inconsistencies.

You'll also participate in training and calibration sessions while contributing feedback to improve rating processes and guidelines.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Evaluate search results and AI-generated content for quality, relevance, accuracy, and usefulness.
  • Conduct online research to verify information and support rating decisions.
  • Apply rating guidelines consistently while maintaining quality standards.
  • Document edge cases, guideline gaps, and task-related issues.
  • Provide clear written feedback and rationale for ratings when required.
  • Participate in training, calibration sessions, and ongoing quality reviews.
  • Meet productivity expectations while maintaining high-quality work.

 

TELUS Digital AI Community

Our global AI Community is a vibrant network of 1 million+ contributors from diverse backgrounds who help our customers collect, enhance, train, translate, and localize content to build better AI models. Become part of our growing community and make an impact supporting the machine learning models of some of the world’s largest brands. 

Qualification path

 

Candidates will complete project-specific training and qualification assessments before joining the program. Ongoing work will be subject to regular quality assurance reviews and performance monitoring.

 

Basic Requirements

  • Working as a freelancer with excellent communication skills in Spanish & English.
  • Resident in Spain for the last 5 consecutive years.
  • Familiarity with current and historical business, media, sports, news, social media, and cultural affairs.
  • Strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, and research skills.
  • Experience using web browsers, search engines, and online research tools.
  • Daily access to a reliable broadband internet connection, smartphone, and personal computer.
  • Demonstrated research capability through professional background OR strong track record of self-directed research and information verification
  • Ability to work independently and follow detailed guidelines consistently.
  • High level of creativity and logical skills with the ability to achieve consistent targets

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in quality assurance, content moderation, data annotation, research, journalism, editing, or information verification.
  • Familiarity with AI technologies, search engines, and digital content ecosystems.
  • Subject matter expertise in areas such as Popular Culture, Social Sciences, STEM, Medicine, Law, Finance, or Engineering.
  • Additional language skills may be beneficial depending on project requirements.

 

Equal Opportunity

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for a contractual relationship without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. At TELUS Digital AI, we are proud to offer equal opportunities and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive community. All aspects of selection are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence, and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.
